Very jumbled, almost incomprehensible memories, but if given enough time, Nux could use those memories to strengthen his understanding of Chaos and by linking it further, Anomaly.
That was all Nux needed.
Time.
And that was what he was trying to buy.
"You are quite arrogant, just like I predicted."
Orravyn’s eyes shined as he scanned Nux with interest.
"Arrogant?
Have you ever been humble in front of creatures you deem beneath you?
Why do you expect me to do the same?"
Nux questioned and the instant he did, instead of getting offended, Orravyn’s smile widened.
It was the exact reaction Nux was looking for.
He hadn’t met any of these Infinities before, but with all the information he had, it wasn’t difficult to understand how twisted their personalities were.
The Infinities loved tormenting those who rose to challenge them.
As for those who looked down upon them, while there hadn’t been a being in the history of the Universe to ever do that—
It was clear that they would want to torment him even more, they would want to make an example out of him and that was exactly what he wanted.
He wanted to lure them into taking their time tormenting him, time that he would use to understand Zylarith’s Fragment’s messy memories and comprehend his Law of Absolute Chaos.
"Creatures you deem beneath you, huh...?
Your perspective of the world would be quite amusing indee—"
Orravyn tried to answer, but just then—
"That is enough."
Zylarith spoke up.
His purple eyes looked right at Orravyn’s face and with a serious look on his face—
"Stop dilly-dallying,
Kill him right now."
Orravyn frowned but before he could do anything, the Infinity of Darkness, Ul’Thakar, grinned out loud.
"Would you look at that~
The great Zylarith Chaosveil is being wary of a child.
Oh, how low the mighty have fallen~"
He chuckled, mocking Zylarith without a tinge of shame.
But Zylarith didn’t lose his temper, instead, he glanced at Ul’Thakar and spoke with a solemn tone.
"The boy is not weak, Ul’Thakar.
He is a threat.
A graver threat than you realize.
I made the same mistake of underestimating him, and I paid the price with half of my Soul.
If it weren’t for her sword, I would have perished."
The one who reacted the most at those words wasn’t the Infinities they were directed to, it was Nux.
HerSword.
He was right.
It was indeed the Seer who had betrayed him.
For now, that didn’t matter, because while the Infinities were having a discussion, all his focus was on Zylarith’s Soul he had devoured.
An hour.
That was all Nux needed.
Well, more accurately, he needed an hour of not fighting, so he could divert all his attention to Zylarith’s fragmented, chaotic and messy memories and make sense out of them.
But if the fight started and his attention shifted—
He would need even more time.
That, however, didn’t seem to be the problem right now because—
"Oh~ The boy’s scary because he defeated me~
As if that’s supposed to make us serious."
The Infinities didn’t seem the least bit bothered by him.

chapters.title: Chapter 2358: Do not underestimate him.
paragraphs: "Oh~ The boy’s scary because he defeated me~
As if that’s supposed to make us serious."
Ul’Thakar mocked Zylarith.
Then, he looked at the one who was once called the Strongest Infinity and with a cold, cruel tone—
"You lost because you were weak."
He spoke directly, his crimson eyes shining with a bright light.
"Not because the boy was strong."
"The boyisstrong.
As much as I hate to admit it, if this were a fair, one-on-one battle, none of us here would have been able to defeat him."
Zylarith did not back down, instead, he looked at the other Infinities and—

"I am not trying to trick any of you, I am saying this because I have seen it with my own eyes. I have seen the boy fight, he wasn’t as strong when he fought against me, in fact, he was weaker than me, so much so that I was looking down on him, just like you are right now.
But he pulled through.
He got stronger the more he fought, till the point I didn’t even realize when he surpassed me.
That is who this boy is.
His strongest suit isn’t his strength or the tricks he has up his sleeves—
It is the rate at which he grows."
Zylarith paused, he looked into Nux’s eyes with... genuine admiration before he turned back to the Infinities and—
"There is a reason a Universe chose him to be its God and in case you are forgetting—
The boy is barely a few thousand years old.
That was all the time he needed to grow from a weak mortal human, to stand in the presence of the Five Strongest Beings in existence and not quiver one bit.
Do not underestimate him."
Zylarith repeated his words.
For a moment, the Infinities stayed silent, Ul’Thakar looked at Nux, as if trying to understand what it was that made Zylarith act the way he was.
But that was when Seraphielle chuckled.
"Stronger than all of us individually? Him?"
The Infinity of Light looked at Zylarith, then at Nux, then she turned back to Zylarith again—
"This is the same boy who didn’t have the guts to stand in our presence and resorted to Guerrilla Warfare."
"He was weaker then."
Zylarith answered calmly.
"Oh? So he got strong enough to defeat us Infinities within a few decades? Is that what you are trying to say?"
Seraphielle raised her eyebrow, as if she wasn’t planning on believing a shred of this fantasy.
"No."
Zylarith shook his head.
Then, he looked at Seraphielle with his purple eyes shining strongly and—
"He got strong enough to defeat us Infinities within a few hours.
Thatis what I am trying to say.
And I am telling you right now, the reason that boy is silently watching us fight each other is because in his mind, he is coming up with a way to get even stronger and win again.
This time, against all of us, together.
And if we continue doing what we are currently doing, we will be handing that victory to him on a silver platter."
Zylarith stressed how important it was, basically giving up his pride and asking the other Four Infinities to come together and fight the threat that would erase them all if they didn’t.
That alone showed how big of a threat he considered Nux to be.
Ul’Thakar noticed it and he narrowed his eyes, for now, he didn’t say anything, Orravyn did.
"Aren’t you overestimating him a little too much? He is a foolish child who made the mistake of trusting someone like her, how dangerous could he be?"
He asked, more out of curiosity than disdain.
"You said it, he is a child who made a mistake, this is the only reason he is here in the first place, if he hadn’t made the mistake he did—
Then he would have been the one attacking us.
And this, I assure you—
If he came to us with full preparation and a plan—
Even if all five of us faced him together—
We would not have won."
Zylarith declared with a serious look on his face, then, he looked at the other Infinities before looking at Orravyn and—
"So be glad he was an inexperienced child who trusted someone he shouldn’t have and take advantage of the mistake he made.
Kill him and remove the threat he poses immediately.
Because if you do not—
We will be the ones who will be erased instead."
Zylarith spoke solemnly, Orravyn wanted to say something, to counter Zylarith in some way, Seraphielle and even Equarios were no different but then—
"Listen to him."
Ul’Thakar spoke up, his crimson eyes shining with a strange understanding.
"Discussions can be done later, we can mock him all we want later, but first—"
The Infinity of Darkness looked at Nux and—
"Let’s get rid of the rat who has been troubling us for decades."
Nux clenched his fists as he looked back at him.
Tsk
He snorted in his mind, but he couldn’t exactly complain, with how strongly Zylarith was trying to convince them, if they didn’t listen to him at this point—
They would be fools.
And however arrogant these Infinities were—
They were not fools.
"Alright then."
And Orravyn proved that as he turned his attention back to Nux.
"Let’s end this."
He spoke as he waved his hand and a relic appeared in the air out of nowhere.
A thin silver page, covered in countless tiny symbols Nux didn’t understand. Orravyn then gently touched the page and the moment he did—
Whoosh
A silent wave spread all over the battlefield, the stars around them dimmed and... the battlefield disappeared from the Universe’s perspective.
When Zylarith sensed it, he looked at Orravyn, somewhat surprised, Orravyn just chuckled.
"You didn’t think we’d be facing him just because you told us to, did you?
We are not your subordinates, Zylarith Chaosveil."

Zylarith looked at him, then he looked at Nux and then at his own hands. Since the Universe couldn’t sense anything that was happening in here, it meant he could use his powers without any restrictions, just like he could back in Nux’s Universe.
It meant he was given a second chance to face Nux and this time, he wasn’t alone.
"That is acceptable."
Zylarith grinned as dense chaos gathered around him and the violet in his eyes shined with a cruel glint.
Nux looked at it, then at Orravyn and his face turned solemn as he realized it.
He wasn’t facing Four Infinities...
He was facing all Five of them.
"You sure prepared a lot to fight a merechild."
He mocked, trying to get a reaction, to buy a few more minutes of time but—
"Prepared?"
Orravyn just laughed with a pitying look on his face and—
"You have no clue, do you?"
That was when Nux’s focus, that had been on Zylarith’s memories, returned to the battlefield all at once.
He clenched his fists, straightened his back and took his battle stance, probably one last time. The Infinities sensed his readiness, and they moved as well.
Seraphielle vanished and appeared right in front of him. Nux blinked in surprise, he didn’t sense any change in the Space around him, that alone told him that the woman did not teleport—
She... moved physically, so fast that even Nux’s eyes couldn’t keep up. Her palm moved towards his chest, light gathered around her, ready to burn him alive—
Nux barely twisted his body at the last instant and teleported a few meters away, his eyes never once left Seraphielle during the entire exchange.
"Hmm? You reacted faster than I expected. I am impressed."
Seraphielle chuckled, a beautiful, almost hypnotic smile appeared on her face, but just then—
SLICE
Her eyes widened in horror as suddenly Ul’Thakar arrived right next to her, blocking an attack that would have cut her head off otherwise.
Or more accurately, blocking the result of an attack that hadn’t happened yet.
An attack whose result arrived before the action.
An impossibility made... possible.
And if it wasn’t for Ul’Thakar arriving at the last second, Seraphielle would have been wounded.
"Hmm.
You were slower than I expected.
I am not impressed."
Nux smiled, looking into her eyes as if he was judging her.
And in an instant, the amused, easy look on Seraphielle’s face changed. She finally realized what Zylarith was talking about, why this monster was... what he was.
Nux didn’t care.
His eyes had already shifted to Ul’Thakar and—
BOOOOM
He punched.
The force struck Ul’Thakar’s chest but his body simply dissolved into mist and the force moved past it, not hurting Ul’Thakar one bit.
Ul’Thakar became solid the next moment.
Nux narrowed his eyes.
Then—
"I am not impressed either."

He heard a voice that came from behind, Nux frowned, he didn’t sense anyone behind him, but as he strengthened his senses, at the very last second, he noticed a very minute mist particle hovering right behind him but by the time he realized what it was—
Ul’Thakar’s body reformed through that mist and he punched.
BOOOOOM
The impact sent Nux flying across the void.
"Khawwwrrkkk!!"
He coughed blood before he spun in the air and stopped himself.
Then, his eyes fell on Ul’Thakar and this little exchange between them was all he needed to understand it.
This one was going to be a problem.

chapters.title: Chapter 2359: You are all creatures I deem beneath myself.
paragraphs: "I am sorry to disappoint you."
Nux commented, looking at Ul’Thakar. The Infinity of Darkness simply waved his hand as if it wasn’t a big deal.
"You aren’t the first, don’t worry about it."
"That is quite generous of you."
Nux smiled as he wiped the blood from his lips.
Then, he vanished and just like Seraphielle, as he did, the Space didn’t react.

The Infinities frowned, was he moving so fast that they couldn’t keep up? But that shouldn’t be possible, he couldn’t react to Seraphielle’s speed, that wouldn’t have happened if he himself was a level faster.
But the Infinities didn’t have the time for answers, because Nux was already in front of Ul’Thakar and—
BOOOOOOM
He punched his head.
Ul’Thakar blurred, the force of his punch passed through mist again, but this time, Nux grinned.
"Grrhhhh!!!"
Ul’Thakar groaned in pain.
A physical attack shouldn’t have hurt him, that should have been impossible but...
Yet again—
Impossible was made possible.
Ul’Thakar’s body reappeared a few meters away, but his head did not. His head had taken permanent damage that would take a long time to heal.
Or at least—
That is what should have happened but then—
Golden Light surrounded Darkness and... inside that Light, Darkness started growing and Ul’Thakar’s head regenerated in an instant.
Seraphielle had healed Ul’Thakar.
"That’s for doing what you did."
She commented, not looking at Ul’Thakar.
Ul’Thakar didn’t say anything either, he just looked at Nux with the same solemn look that Seraphielle had.
"Look at you two, you must get along well, eh?"
Nux tried to taunt, to get a reaction out of them.
He was trying to act cool, like everything was under his control, but that was far from the truth, every single action he was taking took... effort.
The Law of Anomaly was extremely difficult to control.
So much that Nux needed almost all his focus to use it and that made it difficult for him to comprehend Zylarith’s memories.
What would have normally taken less than an hour, at the rate he was going right now, he would need at least a thousand years and that was unacceptable.
He needed to do something.
Anything.
But—
The two Infinities did not react.
Instead—
The Infinity of Balance, Equarios, lifted his hand and then—
A quiet pressure fell over Nux.
The Power of Balance.
And not the weak Balance Nux was used to, it was Balance at its strongest, and it affected even Nux.
Nux had wounded Ul’Thakar, yes.
But he had used impossibility to do so—
ToBalancethat, he needed to pay aPrice.
And that price was what Equarios’s Balance took—
Slice
A thin cut opened on Nux’s shoulder.
"You cannot have an advantage without a payment."
"Is that so..."
Nux kept a strong front as he tried to punch Equarios but—
Then something else happened.
Zylarith moved.
The Energy of Chaos surrounded the path between Nux and Equarios, Nux’s punch forgot where it was supposed to land, and its force moved towards an empty space.
Nux tried to punch again, but a small bronze ring opened beside him.
It was a Relic.
Yes, Orravyn had joined in as well.
Nux’s punch slowed down as the Relic used its power on him, that was when Seraphielle moved again.

But this time, she didn’t directly attack Nux, no, she pushed Ul’Thakar towards him instead, helping him move at her speed. Speed even Nux couldn’t properly react to, Darkness surrounded him in an instant and through that Darkness, Ul’Thakar formed, attacked, and dissolved again.
Nux blocked his blows at the very last second, but Ul’Thakar was physically stronger than him, even after he blocked his attack, the force alone cracked his wrist.
And the worst part?
Ul’Thakar didn’t end it with just one blow—
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM
He continued to attack.
Nux blocked most of his attacks, but the sheer force began to break his body.
Wrists, shoulders, ribs, back, spine—
"Khawwwrrkkkk!!"
One of the attacks sent him flying again, but this time, as Nux stabilized himself midair, he wasn’t even given time to assess his own condition because Ul’Thakar was right behind him.
"Fuck..."
Nux gritted his teeth.
And then—
"FUCK!!"
He screamed as he punched in a random direction and the next instant, the force that came from his punch... multiplied across different positions.
BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM
Thousands of punches aimed at Ul’Thakar, all from different directions, his eyes widened, his body turned into Mist, but again, it did not matter.
"GRRhhhhHh!!"
Ul’Thakar groaned in pain, he tried to reform his body, but this time, it wasn’t just his head that had taken damage, it was most of his body.
But then—
Energy of Balance moved.
For every ’impossible’ punch Nux created, he paid a cost for it.
His muscles tore, his fingers split open, parts of his skin fell apart, his entire body got covered in blood but Nux—
He ignored it all.

He just looked at Ul’Thakar, the Infinity he had specifically targeted. If it was a normal situation, at this point, Ul’Thakar would have already been out of the battle since he would have needed at least half an hour to heal himself—
But as Nux looked at him, Seraphielle was already standing next to him and... his wounds healed in an instant.
Nux stared at the Five Infinities with a solemn look on his face.
This... was not good at all.

These five beings had been each other’s enemies for trillions and trillions of years, so even as they stood in front of him together, he expected their egos to clash against each other’s like it did back when he put Seraphielle in a difficult position and no one came to help her because it benefitted them—
But right now—
Things were exactly the opposite of that.
The Infinities weren’t just fighting individually, they were working together in a way so meticulous that it was impossible for him to find an opening.
Seraphielle kept the group alive, healing whoever was hurt.
Ul’Thakar pressured him physically.
Equarios made every unfair result cost him.
Orravyn used his relics to slow him down and preserved the moments where Nux was forced to struggle.
And Zylarith’s Chaos broke the logic of his Law combinations.
He was not fighting five enemies.
He was... fighting one machine made of Five Infinities.
And it wasn’t going his way.
Nux scanned the battlefield again and then—
His eyes fell on Seraphielle.
If the healer stayed untouched, this would never end.
Seraphielle sensed it immediately and instead of taking the challenge, she moved back at a speed Nux had no way to match.
Not that he needed to.
He simply punched.
BOOOOOOOM
The punch moved through time and appeared where she was going to appear next, Seraphielle sensed something was wrong and tried to change direction.
Zylarith’s Chaos moved to distort Nux’s prediction, Equarios tried to balance the outcome, Orravyn sent a relic to delay Nux’s punch while Ul’Thakar came from the side to attack him.
Nux ignored all of them and—
"Agghh!"
His punch connected with Seraphielle despite all the Infinities’ efforts to stop him, Seraphielle was sent flying.
And Nux, who stood in the middle of the Infinities’ incoming attacks, simply vanished as if he didn’t exist and appeared somewhere far away.
His golden eyes shined with a playful glint as he looked at the Infinities and—
"What’s with the surprise?
I told you before, did I not?
You are all creatures I deem beneath myself."
He grinned.
Then, without looking at anyone in particular—
"Well, I do admit, if it wasn’t for a few of you holding everyone back, you would have had better chances."
He commented.
Again, the goal was to put some form of discord amongst them and gain some time. And for a moment, it seemed like it was working.

Ul’Thakar’s eyes shined at his words as he looked around, Zylarith narrowed his eyes, a few more relics appeared around Orravyn, Equarios adjusted his Grand Scale of Balance, preparing to make Nux pay the price of the impossibility he played with and Seraphielle stabilized herself, golden blood came out from her mouth, but the next instant, it disappeared.
She looked like she was trying to find whose fault it was that she was targeted. Seeing that look on her face, Nux inwardly felt a little hopeful, his trick might work but—
"To think you would try something so childish in front of us.
You really do look down upon us, don’t you?"
Seraphielle looked at him with a surprised smile.
"Well, it’s not exactly the kid’s fault, we did go to War because of him."
Ul’Thakar grinned as well.
"If only they understood how much the two of you crave War."
Orravyn chuckled.
"We don’t exactlycraveit, it’s just fun to let off some steam every once in a while."
Seraphielle explained herself.
Orravyn rolled his eyes.
The rest of the Infinities were the same, all of them were smiling at Nux as if he had no clue where he was.
As for Nux—
He didn’t care.
His mind had shifted its attention to Zylarith’s memories before this conversation even began.
"Alright, enough chit-chat."
Zylarith spoke with a solemn look on his face as even denser Chaos appeared around him, the rest of the Infinities nodded.
Their smiles disappeared as well.
The party time was over.
It was now time to end this.

sentences.text: "I am sorry to disappoint you."
Nux commented, looking at Ul’Thakar.
The Infinity of Darkness simply waved his hand as if it wasn’t a big deal.
"You aren’t the first, don’t worry about it."
"That is quite generous of you."
Nux smiled as he wiped the blood from his lips.
Then, he vanished and just like Seraphielle, as he did, the Space didn’t react.
The Infinities frowned, was he moving so fast that they couldn’t keep up?
But that shouldn’t be possible, he couldn’t react to Seraphielle’s speed, that wouldn’t have happened if he himself was a level faster.
But the Infinities didn’t have the time for answers, because Nux was already in front of Ul’Thakar and—
BOOOOOOM
He punched his head.
Ul’Thakar blurred, the force of his punch passed through mist again, but this time, Nux grinned.
"Grrhhhh!!!"
Ul’Thakar groaned in pain.
A physical attack shouldn’t have hurt him, that should have been impossible but...
Yet again—
Impossible was made possible.
Ul’Thakar’s body reappeared a few meters away, but his head did not.
His head had taken permanent damage that would take a long time to heal.
Or at least—
That is what should have happened but then—
Golden Light surrounded Darkness and... inside that Light, Darkness started growing and Ul’Thakar’s head regenerated in an instant.
Seraphielle had healed Ul’Thakar.
"That’s for doing what you did."
She commented, not looking at Ul’Thakar.
Ul’Thakar didn’t say anything either, he just looked at Nux with the same solemn look that Seraphielle had.
"Look at you two, you must get along well, eh?"
Nux tried to taunt, to get a reaction out of them.
He was trying to act cool, like everything was under his control, but that was far from the truth, every single action he was taking took... effort.
The Law of Anomaly was extremely difficult to control.
So much that Nux needed almost all his focus to use it and that made it difficult for him to comprehend Zylarith’s memories.
What would have normally taken less than an hour, at the rate he was going right now, he would need at least a thousand years and that was unacceptable.
He needed to do something.
Anything.
But—
The two Infinities did not react.
Instead—
The Infinity of Balance, Equarios, lifted his hand and then—
A quiet pressure fell over Nux.
The Power of Balance.
And not the weak Balance Nux was used to, it was Balance at its strongest, and it affected even Nux.
Nux had wounded Ul’Thakar, yes.
But he had used impossibility to do so—
ToBalancethat, he needed to pay aPrice.
And that price was what Equarios’s Balance took—
Slice
A thin cut opened on Nux’s shoulder.
"You cannot have an advantage without a payment."
"Is that so..."
Nux kept a strong front as he tried to punch Equarios but—
Then something else happened.
Zylarith moved.
The Energy of Chaos surrounded the path between Nux and Equarios, Nux’s punch forgot where it was supposed to land, and its force moved towards an empty space.
Nux tried to punch again, but a small bronze ring opened beside him.
It was a Relic.
Yes, Orravyn had joined in as well.
Nux’s punch slowed down as the Relic used its power on him, that was when Seraphielle moved again.
But this time, she didn’t directly attack Nux, no, she pushed Ul’Thakar towards him instead, helping him move at her speed.
Speed even Nux couldn’t properly react to, Darkness surrounded him in an instant and through that Darkness, Ul’Thakar formed, attacked, and dissolved again.
Nux blocked his blows at the very last second, but Ul’Thakar was physically stronger than him, even after he blocked his attack, the force alone cracked his wrist.
And the worst part?
Ul’Thakar didn’t end it with just one blow—
BOOM BOOM BOOM BOOM
He continued to attack.
Nux blocked most of his attacks, but the sheer force began to break his body.
Wrists, shoulders, ribs, back, spine—
"Khawwwrrkkkk!!"
One of the attacks sent him flying again, but this time, as Nux stabilized himself midair, he wasn’t even given time to assess his own condition because Ul’Thakar was right behind him.
"Fuck..."
Nux gritted his teeth.
And then—
"FUCK!!"
He screamed as he punched in a random direction and the next instant, the force that came from his punch... multiplied across different positions.
BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM
Thousands of punches aimed at Ul’Thakar, all from different directions, his eyes widened, his body turned into Mist, but again, it did not matter.
"GRRhhhhHh!!"
Ul’Thakar groaned in pain, he tried to reform his body, but this time, it wasn’t just his head that had taken damage, it was most of his body.
But then—
Energy of Balance moved.
For every ’impossible’ punch Nux created, he paid a cost for it.
His muscles tore, his fingers split open, parts of his skin fell apart, his entire body got covered in blood but Nux—
He ignored it all.
He just looked at Ul’Thakar, the Infinity he had specifically targeted.
If it was a normal situation, at this point, Ul’Thakar would have already been out of the battle since he would have needed at least half an hour to heal himself—
But as Nux looked at him, Seraphielle was already standing next to him and... his wounds healed in an instant.
Nux stared at the Five Infinities with a solemn look on his face.
This... was not good at all.

These five beings had been each other’s enemies for trillions and trillions of years, so even as they stood in front of him together, he expected their egos to clash against each other’s like it did back when he put Seraphielle in a difficult position and no one came to help her because it benefitted them—
But right now—
Things were exactly the opposite of that.
The Infinities weren’t just fighting individually, they were working together in a way so meticulous that it was impossible for him to find an opening.
Seraphielle kept the group alive, healing whoever was hurt.
Ul’Thakar pressured him physically.
Equarios made every unfair result cost him.
Orravyn used his relics to slow him down and preserved the moments where Nux was forced to struggle.
And Zylarith’s Chaos broke the logic of his Law combinations.
He was not fighting five enemies.
He was... fighting one machine made of Five Infinities.
And it wasn’t going his way.
Nux scanned the battlefield again and then—
His eyes fell on Seraphielle.
If the healer stayed untouched, this would never end.
Seraphielle sensed it immediately and instead of taking the challenge, she moved back at a speed Nux had no way to match.
Not that he needed to.
He simply punched.
BOOOOOOOM
The punch moved through time and appeared where she was going to appear next, Seraphielle sensed something was wrong and tried to change direction.
Zylarith’s Chaos moved to distort Nux’s prediction, Equarios tried to balance the outcome, Orravyn sent a relic to delay Nux’s punch while Ul’Thakar came from the side to attack him.
Nux ignored all of them and—
"Agghh!"
His punch connected with Seraphielle despite all the Infinities’ efforts to stop him, Seraphielle was sent flying.
And Nux, who stood in the middle of the Infinities’ incoming attacks, simply vanished as if he didn’t exist and appeared somewhere far away.
His golden eyes shined with a playful glint as he looked at the Infinities and—
"What’s with the surprise?
I told you before, did I not?
You are all creatures I deem beneath myself."
He grinned.
Then, without looking at anyone in particular—
"Well, I do admit, if it wasn’t for a few of you holding everyone back, you would have had better chances."
He commented.
Again, the goal was to put some form of discord amongst them and gain some time.
And for a moment, it seemed like it was working.

Ul’Thakar’s eyes shined at his words as he looked around, Zylarith narrowed his eyes, a few more relics appeared around Orravyn, Equarios adjusted his Grand Scale of Balance, preparing to make Nux pay the price of the impossibility he played with and Seraphielle stabilized herself, golden blood came out from her mouth, but the next instant, it disappeared.
She looked like she was trying to find whose fault it was that she was targeted.
Seeing that look on her face, Nux inwardly felt a little hopeful, his trick might work but—
"To think you would try something so childish in front of us.
You really do look down upon us, don’t you?"
Seraphielle looked at him with a surprised smile.
"Well, it’s not exactly the kid’s fault, we did go to War because of him."
Ul’Thakar grinned as well.
"If only they understood how much the two of you crave War."
Orravyn chuckled.
"We don’t exactlycraveit, it’s just fun to let off some steam every once in a while."
Seraphielle explained herself.
Orravyn rolled his eyes.
The rest of the Infinities were the same, all of them were smiling at Nux as if he had no clue where he was.
As for Nux—
He didn’t care.
His mind had shifted its attention to Zylarith’s memories before this conversation even began.
"Alright, enough chit-chat."
Zylarith spoke with a solemn look on his face as even denser Chaos appeared around him, the rest of the Infinities nodded.
Their smiles disappeared as well.
The party time was over.
It was now time to end this.

chapters.title: Chapter 2360: Law of Anomaly.
paragraphs: Seraphielle raised her hand and Light spread outward, wrapping around the other four Infinities, even Zylarith.

Their movements became faster, their recovery quickened and using the new buff, Ul’Thakar rushed in, Zylarith’s Chaos followed behind him, twisting every path Nux could take, Equarios imposed Balance over the whole battlefield, three of Orravyn’s relics moved at once.
A silver chain to bind Nux.
A black tablet to preserve Nux’s wounds, making it impossible to heal them.
A broken crystal eye to record his movements.
Nux’s thoughts returned to him and he punched, this time, the Law of Destruction was infused into the Force his punch generated.
And he destroyed the silver chain that came to bind him.
Or at least...
That’s what Nux thought would happen but—
Even with the Chain shattered, it moved towards Nux, binding him.
Nux’s eyes widened in surprise, Orravyn, on the other hand, just smiled.
This was Orravyn Eternity’s Law.
The Law of Absolute Archive.
It gave him the power to record, preserve, store, reproduce, study, and weaponize anything that could be known.

To Orravyn, knowledge was not just information. Knowledge was power, structure, memory, and reality. If something had happened, if a Law had been used, if an attack had taken form, if a Primordial Energy had moved in a certain pattern, Orravyn could record it inside his Archive and once something was recorded, it was no longer lost to time.
He could preserve it, recreate it, seal it inside a relic, or use it as a counter later.

This was what made him so terrifying, his Relics were not normal weapons, they were physical ’pages’ of his Archive, one relic may contain a recorded attack from the past, another may replay a moment, seal a movement, store a Law pattern, or reproduce the effect of a Primordial Energy.
So even now, as Nux destroyed his Relic, his Archive still preserved its function, allowing the relic to move and fulfil its function till it was erased from the Universe.
One second.
That was all Orravyn’s broken chain could buy him and that second was enough since Ul’Thakar was here and—
BOOOOM
His punch covered with endless darkness struck Nux’s stomach.
"Kkhkarrkkkk!!!"
Nux’s body folded as he coughed blood, Seraphielle appeared behind him as Light burned his body, Zylarith’s Chaos twisted the impact, making the pain even more severe—
"RRAAAAHHHH!!!"
Nux roared as he punched Ul’Thakar. The Infinity of Darkness scattered, but the attack damaged him anyway.
"Grrhh."
Ul’Thakar groaned in pain. Equarios moved to balance the damage, half of it shifted from Ul’Thakar to Nux.
"Krrkhhrrr!"
Nux coughed blood again.
He tried to move back, but Orravyn’s relic slowed him again, just for a moment, but that was enough, Seraphielle, Ul’Thakar, Zylarith, all moved.
All three attacks came together, Nux clenched his fists, then, his golden eyes burned brightly as the Power of Anomaly flared in his desperate attempt.
The attacks that should have landed did not.
Instead, Nux was now standing behind Ul’Thakar and—
BOOOOOOOOOM
He punched.
This time, the punch carried Space, Time, Destruction, Chaos, Death and Anomaly and—
"AAAAAAGGGGHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"
Ul’Thakar screamed in agony.

This time, his body couldn’t even dissolve to scatter the damage, the Destruction kept the wound open, Death made it deadly, Chaos made it painful, Time slowed the moment so Ul’Thakar felt it even more, Space locked him down and Anomaly—
Anomaly made it all, which should have been impossible, possible.
More than half of Ul’Thakar’s body was erased out of existence and Nux didn’t waste time, he tried to punch again.
The same punch, with the same powers, and if it landed—
Ul’Thakar Darkness would perish.

Ul’Thakar’s eyes widened, others moved instantly, Seraphielle tried to heal him, but Nux declared it to be impossible. Equarios stepped in, trying to deal with the impossibility, but before he could, Nux left Ul’Thakar and appeared behind Equarios, ready to end him instead.
Or at least—
That’s what he wanted.
But the Chaos twisted his Path.
Nux moved to an open space where he couldn’t attack any of the Infinities directly and both Ul’Thakar and Equarios lived.
"Khharrrkkkkk!!"
Nux coughed blood.
The Power of Balance took the price.

His body felt weak, blood came from his mouth, his chest was open, his arms were torn, but his eyes, his golden eyes shined as he glared at Ul’Thakar, who would need at least a few hours to return to his original state and this time, Seraphielle wouldn’t be able to help him.
"That felt good..."
He spoke with a bloodied grin as he looked at the Infinity of Darkness.
Ul’Thakar’s face twisted.
The other Infinities stared at Nux, and no one spoke for a moment.
He had injured an Infinity, and it wasn’t a light injury or a fluke, if Nux had half a second longer, an Infinity would have fallen today.
That thought alone made the Infinities’ blood run cold.
"Do not give him another opening."
Zylarith spoke with a solemn look on his face and this time, not a single Infinity mocked him because what they just saw made them realize what sort of monster they were fighting.

Seraphielle’s Light grew brighter, Equarios’ Balance formed an even tighter grip in the void, Orravyn summoned five more relics, and Ul’Thakar, while he had shifted to the sidelines for a while, his crimson eyes were constantly looking for payback.
And Nux—
He looked at his enemies and with his broken body—
He took his battle stance again.
The Five Infinities moved together without a shred of pride or dignity.
They no longer cared how it looked.
They no longer attacked one by one.
They no longer gave him space.
Five Infinities, Five Strongest Beings in the Universe, shamelessly surrounded one man, a boy who wasn’t even a tenth of their age—
And then they began to crush him.

Seraphielle’s Light moved first, making every attack faster. Ul’Thakar’s Darkness formed fists, claws, knees, and elbows, all landing on him with terrifying force and breaking Nux’s body even further.
Zylarith’s Chaos made it impossible for Nux to even understand where he was, Equarios made it so using the Power of Anomaly became tougher and tougher.
And Orravyn watched, his Archive turned, recording every single thing, and the more the battle continued, the more he understood Nux’s matters, the more he began... predicting him.
As for Nux—
He fought back.
He fought Seraphielle’s Light that moved faster than he could react to.
He fought against Ul’Thakar’s attacks that were slowly breaking his body apart.
He fought Zylarith’s Chaos that poisoned meaning itself.
He fought Equarios’ Balance that punished every impossible answer.
He fought Orravyn’s Archive that recorded, preserved, and used every weakness it saw.
And as he continued to fight in that state for hours—
Something inside him... started to change.
He had been using the Law of Anomaly since the battle had begun, the very reason he could even stand in front of these ridiculously strong beings was because the Law of Anomaly made it possible.
The only reason his attacks worked was because the Law of Anomaly made them work.
He used it to survive attacks he should not have survived, he had used it to move when he shouldn’t be able to, strike even when the attack itself had failed, and create results without proper cause.

At the beginning of the battle, he needed to think, he needed to decide what impossible thing he wanted to make real, how he was supposed to do it, how much energy it would take, he needed to calculate it, think of the most efficient way possible, think what effect it would have, whatpricehe would need to pay—
But now, after so long, after so many clashes, the Power of Anomaly and Impossibility, all the calculations that his head did knowingly started coming to him... instinctively.
Yes, Zenith Flow.
His body, that was trained to move on its own every time he fought, started doing the same on its own and this time—
It started doing it with theLaw of Anomaly.

And because of that, Nux could finally do what he had been trying to do all this while, he shifted a part of his focus away from the battle, to Zylarith’s scattered, broken, fragmented memories, and he began to make sense of them.
Three hours.
That was what he needed.
Three hours to filter them, to arrange them and to comprehend whatever Zylarith’s Soul could give him.
So Nux fought.
And while he fought, he read.
But—
He couldn’t exactly let go either.
Even with all his attention, the Infinities were still injuring him, now that some of his attention was gone—
It was worse.
Ul’Thakar broke his ribs again and again.
Seraphielle’s Light tore through his shoulder and healed her allies every time Nux managed to injure them.
Zylarith’s Chaos made his wounds worsen in strange ways.
Equarios made every impossible act cost more than the last.
Orravyn’s relics preserved injuries that should have closed.
Every time Nux bled, he healed.
Every time his body was broken, he forced it straight.
Every time he was thrown, he returned.
His arms shook from the pressure, his breathing grew heavier, but his eyes burned brighter and brighter.
The fight continued.
Minutes became half an hour.
Half an hour became one hour.
One hour became two.
For two full hours, Nux fought the Five Infinities.
And the longer he fought—
The sharper his instincts became.

chapters.title: Chapter 2361: “Kill me.”
paragraphs: For two full hours, Nux fought the Five Infinities.
And the longer he fought—
The sharper his instincts became.
His body started handling the battle with less and less thought, he no longer needed to consciously force every impossible result.
The Power of Anomaly moved with him, even his breathing itself carried the power of Impossibility.
Even the Infinities could feel it.
Nux was exhausted.
He was injured, he was bleeding, externally and internally, his body was screaming in agony, yet somehow...
The Infinities weren’t able to land the final blow.
In fact, it was becoming harder and harder to kill him.
But Infinities were still... Infinities.
They didn’t stop.
Their thought process was simple, it didn’t matter if they couldn’t land the final blow, all they needed to do was to keep landing blows until one of thembecamethe final blow.
And that was what they did.
Without any mercy, they moved in the same formation, not giving Nux even an instant to breathe or collect himself.
Any small opening they found, they used it and just like that, Nux’s injuries kept piling up.

His left arm stopped healing at all, his ribs were broken in too many places to even be recognized as ribs, one of his lungs had collapsed and was only healed halfway, his right leg had no proper feeling left, his blood drifted around him in red streams.
His body was... ruined.
He was... barely hanging on.
And the Infinities didn’t show any intention of stopping. At this point, they didn’t even talk, Nux tried to rile them up, taunt them or pit them against each other—
But ever since he injured Ul’Thakar that time, an injury that had already healed because of Orravyn’s Relics, the Infinities never once said a word.
It was clear.
They were not going to stop until Nux was down.
So...
In that moment, Nux made a decision.
He let go.
He let go of the control he had on his body, more than ninety-five percent of his focus shifted onto Zylarith’s memories.
Only a thin part of his mind stayed with his body, a little awareness he still needed to use the Power of Anomaly and actually know what was happening.
As for the rest—
It was gone.
And the effect was instant.
The time he needed dropped.
The remaining hour became ten minutes.
Yes.
Ten more minutes.
If he could last ten more minutes, he would stand a chance.
With that—
His body continued fighting, almost entirely on instinct alone.
His body turned, he used his Laws, he punched, his Law of Anomaly flared and faded, flared and faded, answering threats without waiting for full thought.
And like that—
More time passed.
One minute.
Two minutes.
Three minutes.
His instincts were still moving him, but his body could no longer keep up.
Even impossibility needed a vessel and Nux’s vessel was... breaking.
That was when one of Ul’Thakar’s blows sent him flying backwards, crushing his already broken ribs.
Nux tried to stop himself, but his body did not answer properly.
Seraphielle appeared above him, Spears of Light rained down on him, Nux twisted his body, trying to dodge but—
He was too slow.
One of the spears cut through his shoulder, Zylarith’s Chaos entered the wound and made the pain worse, almost paralyzing Nux’s right arm.
Equarios raised his hand.
Nux was moving when it shouldn’t be possible, his body was no longer in the state to move, the only reason he could move was because—
He had made the impossible possible.
And for that—
He needed to pay the price.
CRACK
The bones in both his legs were crushed.
"Frrhhhh!"
Nux coughed out blood, his body was ruptured from the pressure, but he kept moving, he kept... surviving.
Seven more minutes...
Only seven.
That seven became six.
Six became five.
Five became four.
And four became... three.
Three minutes.
Only three more minutes.
That was all Nux needed.
He moved his ruined body even as it twitched lifelessly, his trembling fingers curled and formed a punch.
But—
That was when it happened.
Orravyn appeared behind the already ruined Nux, holding a small, almost plain-looking relic in his hand.
A black rectangular plate. Orravyn placed it on Nux’s back and—
"Recorded Stillness."
The instant those words were said, the relic activated. Its surface, which was covered with countless small pale symbols, shined and—
FWOOOM
It released a pressure so terrifying that Nux felt threatened.
He tried to move away, but it was already too late.
CLINK CLINK CLINK
The Relic was already activated, black chains erupted from it and wrapped around Nux, not around his body, but around his... current state.
His exhausted, injured, slowed, surrounded state.
That state was then recorded properly and Orravyn’s Archive declared it to be true.
The moment that happened—
Nux’s body froze.
His eyes sharpened instantly, a part of his mind snapped back from Zylarith’s memories, his arm trembled, the Power of Anomaly gathered around him and for one instant—
Crack
The Chains binding him cracked, it looked like he would be able to force his way out of it through the power of Impossibility but just then—
Orravyn waved his hands and... more relics moved.

A silver ring locked around his right wrist, a golden nail pierced the space near his left shoulder, a white thread wrapped around his throat without touching skin, a black chain coiled around his legs, a broken mirror appeared before his chest, a small bronze clock stopped above his head.
Every single relic added another binding.
One sealed movement.
One sealed Space.
One delayed Time.
One preserved injury.
One blocked his form from using his Laws.
One recorded every failed escape and repeated it.
"LET ME GO!!"
Nux’s scream came out distorted since his throat was torn, his eyes flared, the golden light in them shined more intensely than ever.
The Power of Impossibility gathered, the binding relics around him trembled, almost as if they could no longer hold him.
For one terrifying moment, Nux nearly forced his way out but—
That was when a vast, unseen scale appeared over the battlefield, Nux’s eyes glared at it and—
"Balance."
Equarios spoke calmly.
The scale tilted.
On one side was Nux’s escape.
On the other side was the price required to make that escape real.
And the price continued to rise.
Ul’Thakar, Seraphielle and Zylarith closed in, adding themselves to the factor, the scale tilted even more, the price rose even further—
Until it became clear.
If Nux used the Power of Impossibility to break out now—
The price would be his very life.
And Nux realized it in an instant—
It wasn’t just histhislife, he wouldn’t be able to revive from his wives’ shadows. No, that was not how it worked.
If he accepted this price, he would willingly be giving away his existence.
Not as a being—
But as a Universe.
Meaning this price wasn’t his own life, it was his entire Universe and every single being that existed in there.
Of course, the Infinities did not know it, not even Equarios, after all, even now, they still did not understand what sort of existence Nux even was.
Equarios just looked at him without emotion and—
"Impossible outcomes require... an impossible payment."
He declared coldly.
And Nux...
He stopped resisting.
The price was too high, he couldn’t pay it.
So he... gave in.
His golden eyes, that were shining intensely lost their light, then, he looked at the Five Infinities who surrounded him and he... grinned for one last time.
"It took five of you..."
He spoke, his voice was so hoarse that his words barely made sense, but the Infinities understood it.
"Five of you... to defeat me..."
"Indeed."
Orravyn nodded.
"You were stronger than we thought."

The Infinity of Eternity admitted and none of the other Infinities scoffed at it. Even Ul’Thakar was no exception, all this while, in his mind, he had always believed that after Zylarith at his prime, he was the strongest being in existence—
But seeing this... boy with a ruined body bound in front of him, that thought had changed.
He wasn’t the strongest.
Neither was Zylarith at his peak the strongest.
It was him.
Nux Leander was the strongest being in the history of their Universe.
Ul’Thakar admitted it openly and so did all the other Infinities.
But—
That didn’t matter.
Because despite being the strongest—
Nux Leander lost.
They won.
It was over.
And Nux knew that.
So he looked at the five beings in front of him one last time and—
"Kill me."
He spoke in a weak, hoarse, almost... powerless voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 2362: Stop it.
paragraphs: [Kill me.]
The wives, who were watching everything happening in the Main Universe through Nux’s eyes, felt their hearts being pierced by thousands of needles when they heard those words.
NOOOOO!!!
NUXX!!!"
Amaya lost herself, the devouring energy around her flared, the Progenitors appeared around her, trying to calm her down or stop her from doing anything foolish but—
BOOOOOOOOM
Her devouring energy flared, pushing all the Progenitors away, then, her energy began to tear open the Universe’s Walls, opening a way towards Nux so she could go and help him.
Or at least...
That was the intention but...
Amaya, or any other woman here in general, was simply too weak to break the Walls between the Universes and leave.
This was also the reason Vyriana, Astaria, Sharnoth, Aeliana and every other woman just... stared at the screen in front of them with hollow looks on their faces.
Because—
They had already tried what Amaya was trying to do.
And they failed as well.
The women couldn’t leave.
Nux had made it impossible from the very beginning.
Azriel watched the scene in front of him through a screen, he watched his daughter kneeling on the ground with that dried, empty, dead look on her face and...
There was nothing he could do.
He wanted to help, he wanted to fight together with Nux, even when he knew he wouldn’t be of much help and would probably only get in the way, he wanted to be there but—
He was the Universe’s Child.
And Orravyn...
The Infinity of Eternity made it impossible for the Universe or any being connected to the Universe to know about what was happening and where it was happening.
The worst part?

He couldn’t even expand his senses and search on his own, because now that his senses were connected with the Universe, the moment he found out what was happening and where it was happening, the Universe would too and before he would be able to do anything—
The Universe itself would crush Nux and erase his existence.
Azriel was... completely sidelined and that made him clench his fists in anger.
If only...
If only he hadn’t abandoned his powers and Yrniel.
If only he was as strong as he once was.
If only he wasn’t connected to the Universe like he was right now.
And as he thought about all this—
He couldn’t help but recall that woman’s face.
The Seer.
She came to him centuries ago, made him abandon his powers and become the Universe’s Child.
At first, he thought it was a second chance, a chance to get his wives back.
But only now did he realize that it was nothing more than that woman’s trap to make it impossible for him to interfere in this situation and help the man his daughter loved.
It made him feel... numb.
Just how long had that woman been planning this for...?
Just... how many possibilities did she predict...?
All these questions were there, in some part of his head, but right now—
His focus was entirely on his broken daughter as he dreaded what she might do.
That was when it happened—
"It’s over."
Azriel heard a voice.
It was Amaya.
All this while, the woman had been attacking the Universe Wall with all her might, but at this point, even she could see it wouldn’t do anything.
So...
She made another decision.
"Instead of watching him die—"
She spoke and as she did, Azriel’s blood went cold because... he could see his daughter was listening to her with that intense, determined look in her eyes.
"I will be going first and wait for him."
Amaya declared, Aeliana’s eyes shined at those words, liking that idea more and more, Azriel’s eyes widened in horror, he tried to say something, to stop them, but before he could—
"Don’t be foolish."
Another voice was heard.
Azriel quickly turned and his eyes fell on her.
Shadow.

Shadow was the only woman who hadn’t moved from her spot ever since the battle started, she didn’t try to attack the boundaries of the Universe, neither did she try to kill herself, she just... watched.
But the moment Amaya’s devouring energy surrounded her, Shadow made it stop and looked right into her sister’s eyes.
"He hasn’t lost yet."
And those words made every single woman present there react.
"What...?"
Amaya’s expression changed, her Devouring Mist disappeared in an instant as she now stared at Shadow with an intense, hopeful look on her face.
"I said, he didn’t lose."
Shadow repeated slowly, making every single one of her words clear.
[What are you saying...?]
Azriel asked, looking at Shadow for answers.
The women were the same, Shadow looked at all of them and—
"Don’t you see?
We are still alive, that means Nux hasn’t lost."
When the women heard those words, their eyes shined with enlightenment and hope, Azriel on the other hand, was even more confused.
[What does that...]
He tried to ask.
Shadow looked at him and—
"Nux is our Universe, if he perishes, his Universe and beings connected to his Universe perish with him."
She started explaining.
Azriel nodded, that much he knew.
"Nux knows that as well, he knows our lives are connected to his, he knows that if he dies, we die too."
The Vampire Progenitor nodded again, even now, he was still following.
"But... he didn’t die.
He let himself be captured.
Why would he do that?
Why would he let himself be captured when he knows the Infinities could reach his wives through him?"
That was when Azriel realized it as well.
Why would he do it...?

As far as he knew Nux, in a situation like this, he would very much end everything right here instead of getting his wives captured and tormented, which, the Infinities would do the instant they realized how valuable they were to him.
Then...
Why didn’t he end everything...?
Azriel thought about it for a moment and the answer became clearer.
[He has a way out.]
He muttered and Shadow grinned.
She looked up, at the Energy of Chaos that was becoming denser and denser and her grin widened.
"Two more minutes."
She declared.
"Two more minutes are all Nux needs."
Yes, that was what he had been planning, the moment Orravyn captured him and he realized he couldn’t escape—
Nux played the role of a defeated enemy, an enemy who was prepared to go down, but he wanted to go down with pride.

This was also the reason he was talking to the Infinities in the first place, he wanted time, he wanted them to talk to him, manipulate them into giving a farewell speech, or saying something like how he made a mistake of fighting them and whatnot.
Even torture, even if the Infinities decided to break him mentally, to take away his ’last wish’ of a prideful death and decided to make him scream till he begged for death—
Anything would work.
As long as it held for three minutes.
And it worked.
The moment he asked the Infinities to kill him, they smiled—
"Kill you? You really are young and naïve, huh..."
Seraphielle chuckled as she gently cupped his cheek with her hand with a gentle look on her face.

The rest of the Infinities looked at him with smiles as well. They all knew what was going to happen, they all knew what Seraphielle did when she had this ’gentleness’ on her face and for the first time in maybe trillions and trillions of years—
None of the Infinities felt disgusted by it.
Instead, they were looking forward to it.
They were looking forward to how Seraphielle was going to break him, in fact, they participated in it.
"He is indeed."
Ul’Thakar laughed.
"He really believed death would be the end of it."
The Infinity of Darkness grinned.
"We are not going to kill you, Nux Leander.
That would be too easy."
Zylarith spoke up, hovering towards him as his violet eyes shined brightly.
"We are going to use you to make our way to the Universe you came from, we are going to learn your secrets, we are going to find every single thing you have been hiding..."
The Infinities continued—
Explaining every single thing they were going to do with him, slowly and properly, making sure they noted his expressions to the last second.
Nux played his role very well too, he tried to remain strong, but he let his fear ’leak’ from time to time, giving the five the satisfaction that they were winning.
When the wives saw what he was doing, they couldn’t help but smile.
Two minutes.
That was all Nux needed.
Nux stuttered, looking at the Five with horrified eyes, the Infinities grinned.
"Oh this is just the begin—"
Zylarith tried to speak, to cut him off, to fill his eyes with dread but just then—
"Stop it."
Another voice was heard.
"It is embarrassing to see your lot made fools by a mere child."
The Seer was here.

Even torture, even if the Infinities decided to break him mentally, to take away his ’last wish’ of a prideful death and decided to make him scream till he begged for death—
Anything would work.
As long as it held for three minutes.
And it worked.
The moment he asked the Infinities to kill him, they smiled—
"Kill you?
You really are young and naïve, huh..."
Seraphielle chuckled as she gently cupped his cheek with her hand with a gentle look on her face.
The rest of the Infinities looked at him with smiles as well.
They all knew what was going to happen, they all knew what Seraphielle did when she had this ’gentleness’ on her face and for the first time in maybe trillions and trillions of years—
None of the Infinities felt disgusted by it.
Instead, they were looking forward to it.
They were looking forward to how Seraphielle was going to break him, in fact, they participated in it.
"He is indeed."
Ul’Thakar laughed.
"He really believed death would be the end of it."
The Infinity of Darkness grinned.
"We are not going to kill you, Nux Leander.
That would be too easy."
Zylarith spoke up, hovering towards him as his violet eyes shined brightly.
"We are going to use you to make our way to the Universe you came from, we are going to learn your secrets, we are going to find every single thing you have been hiding..."
The Infinities continued—
Explaining every single thing they were going to do with him, slowly and properly, making sure they noted his expressions to the last second.
Nux played his role very well too, he tried to remain strong, but he let his fear ’leak’ from time to time, giving the five the satisfaction that they were winning.
When the wives saw what he was doing, they couldn’t help but smile.
Two minutes.
That was all Nux needed.
Nux stuttered, looking at the Five with horrified eyes, the Infinities grinned.
"Oh this is just the begin—"
Zylarith tried to speak, to cut him off, to fill his eyes with dread but just then—
"Stop it."
Another voice was heard.
"It is embarrassing to see your lot made fools by a mere child."
The Seer was here.

chapters.title: Chapter 2363: I WILL KILL HER!!!
paragraphs: "Oh this is just the begin—"
Zylarith tried to speak, to cut him off, to fill his eyes with dread but just then—
"Stop it."
Another voice was heard.
Zylarith and the other Infinities turned around to see who it was and their eyes fell on a beautiful woman they recognized very well.
It was the Seer.
"Why are you here?"
Zylarith asked as he narrowed his eyes.
"And what do you mean stop?"
Seraphielle was the same. She looked at the woman and—
"The deal was that you give us the Anomaly and we give you Vashti’s body and Soul back. You have no right to be here or decide what we do to him."
The Infinity of Light repeated the terms.
The Seer looked at her for a moment and then—
"Yes. That was indeed our deal."
She nodded.
"But that deal only stands when you lot come out of this alive."
"Are you... threatening us?"
Ul’Thakar narrowed his eyes.
The Seer simply shook her head.
"I have no desire to do that.
At this point, you should know that well."

The woman then looked past the Infinities and her eyes fell on Nux, who was glaring at her with strong hatred and this time, he wasn’t pretending. He truly was angry, angry enough to make him want to tear this woman apart and torture her for the rest of Eternity but...
The Seer didn’t care.
She just looked back at Ul’Thakar and—
"I am talking about him."
She spoke as she pointed at Nux.
"THAT BITCH!!!"
On the other side, Amaya, who had been watching everything from the other side, screamed in rage as she heard the Seer’s words.
The women weren’t fools.
The moment they saw her appear, that too, just when Nux was about to get what he wanted and successfully fool the Infinities, they knew why she was here.
They just... for some reason, they hoped that she didn’t know, that she came here to join in the ’fun’, to... torment Nux and gloat about her victory...
But—
"Him?"
Ul’Thakar frowned. Then, he looked at Nux and looked back at Seer and laughed.
"What could he even do? Look at him."
The Infinity of Darkness was confident.
And he wasn’t alone, all the Infinities, even Zylarith, were the same.
The Seer looked at them, especially at Zylarith and—
"It is embarrassing to see your lot made fools by a mere child."
She spoke and in an instant, the void turned silent. The Infinities narrowed their eyes, Ul’Thakar had already clenched his fists, as if he was barely holding himself back from attacking her.
But Zylarith was different.
"What are you trying to say?"
He asked directly.
"What can he even do now?"
"You, of all people, are asking that?"
The Seer questioned back.
"Did you forget what happened when you went against him?"
Zylarith didn’t say anything, for some reason, he felt like the more he spoke here, the bigger fool he would look like.
That was when the Seer asked a question that changed Zylarith’s expression.
"Where is the rest of your Soul, Zylarith?"
"It was erased."
Zylarith answered with an ugly look on his face, but the Seer’s tone only got stricter.
"That is not what I am asking,
I askedwherethe rest of it is.
It certainly didn’t return to our Universe thenwherewas it erased?"
She asked.
"Inside his..."
Zylarith turned towards Nux and answered, however, mid-sentence, he paused as he realized what she was talking about and his eyes widened in horror.
"It is with him."
The Seer on the other hand, only nodded.
"Right now, he is most likely trying to read through your memories, understand and steal your Law and your understanding of it and if he succeeds..."
The Seer paused for a short moment as she looked at the rest of the shocked Infinities and—
"You won’t just be facing the Anomaly, you will be facing an Anomaly who has completely absorbed Zylarith Chaosveil and knows everything he does."
She then specifically looked at Ul’Thakar and—
"And that is not a battle any of us would survive."
"Any ofus...?"
Orravyn raised his eyebrow, noticing something he had never once noticed in the Seer’s tone.
Fear.

"What? You think once he obliterates you lot and takes over the Universe, he would let me go? I never feared any of you because I knew none of you had what it takes to defeat the other three and rule the Universe—"
The Seer spoke without a shred of discretion, she truly did not care because none of the five here could actually do anything to her.
But...
As she turned towards the captured Nux, who was still glaring at her with that same intense hatred even now—
"But he is different."
She lowered her voice.
"So do all of us a favor and...
Get rid of him.
Now."
She commanded and—
"I WILL KILL HER!!!"
Amaya screamed, feeling rage she had never felt in her entire life as she glanced at that bitch through the screen.
And this time, she wasn’t alone.
Every single woman, even Shadow, was the same.
They all felt the same hatred towards the Seer that Amaya did but—
"Calm down."

This time, Felberta was the one who raised her voice. Her words came out in a hoarse tone, it looked as if she could cry any moment now, but the woman held back her tears and looked at the screen with brave, moist eyes—
"We are still alive."
She spoke, repeating what Shadow said before, just with more conviction.
"Nux is our Universe, if something happens to him, we all perish, he knows that, so the fa—"
But—
Just as Felberta was about to say how the fact they were alive meant Nux had a plan, that he would rather have every single one of them die than be tormented for the rest of their lives—
Something else happened.
Zzpp
The screen they were watching everything from disappeared and the women’s expressions changed.
They...
They could no longer sense Nux’s presence.

chapters.title: Chapter 2364: Please live on.
paragraphs: Zzpp
The screen they were watching everything from disappeared and the women’s expressions changed.
They...
They could no longer sense Nux’s presence.
Felberta froze, not even completing her words. The rest of the women all stood up, they tried to sense their connection, even if they had to force it.
But—
No matter what they did.
It didn’t happen.
And that was... terrifying.
This had never happened before.

Even when Nux was trapped in the Temple of Time, while they couldn’t talk to him, the wives could still sense he was alive, their connection was still there, this was the only reason they even remained sane.
But now...
The connection was gone.
And no matter how much they tried to reform it, they weren’t able to.
It was almost as if...
Nux had perished.
But—
This shouldn’t be possible!"
Shadow raised her voice.
"Nux is our Universe, if something happened to him, the Universe shouldn’t be fi—"
However, before she could even complete her sentence—
Zzp
Another screen appeared in front of the women, all of them turned towards it desperately and there he was—
Nux.
But...
The women’s expressions didn’t ease after seeing him because—
"That’s a recording..."
Riona commented with a hollow look on her face.
And the recording started speaking—
"If you are seeing this...
Then I apologize."
Nux spoke with a heavy look on his face.
The women looked at the screen, those few sentences were more than enough for their minds to understand what had happened, their hearts, however, refused to believe it.
Not that they had a choice and what Nux in the recording spoke next only slapped the truth right in front of them.
"I was too arrogant and I made a mistake.
I underestimated Zylarith and... I paid the price for it."
He paused, almost as if he was collecting himself, then, he gulped softly, his golden eyes shining brightly—
"But in my last moment, please fulfil my one, final selfish desire."
He spoke, his eyes turning moist.
"Please live on."
Nux then looked at all his wives—
"I love every single one of you, I cherish you more than anything, and every single day of my life, I had been grateful for having all of you by my side.
But—
My heart is not strong enough to take on the burden of ending your life, with my own.
I am not that strong.
I have... never been that strong.
So—
I passed everything I have to Shadow.

From now on, she is the Universe, she is its sole ruler, she is the one who keeps it alive. At the same time, I have closed our Universe from any form of Multiverse Travel, no being from any Universe would be able to enter our Universe, neither will you be able to leave yours.
I apologize for trapping you inside, but this was the only way I had to ensure none of you lose yourselves in the feeling of revenge."
Nux then moved closer to the screen and spoke in a more convincing tone—
"Live."
He repeated himself.
"For our children.
Be with them, do not curse them with the life of an orphan because of my mistake.
They do not deserve that."
Nux then paused.
From the very beginning, he knew none of his wives would be willing to live without him, neither was he asking them to do it for Eternity.
He only wanted them to be there for their children, but now that the Universe was closed, and the children had no way to grow any further and achieve immortality—
Nux knew that the instant their children’s lifespans ended, his wives would follow.
So he looked at his wives through the screen, and he smiled one last time.
"And while you are there, raising those little things.
I will take over the underworld and make it a better place for when you and our children come here."
He joked, knowing something like the ’underworld’ did not exist.
Then, his eyes turned moist and—
"May we reunite in death."
Zzzp
The moment he said those words, the recording ended and—
Silence.
Absolute silence fell over Nux’s Universe.
None of the women said anything, if before, their hearts refused to accept the reality, now, they had no choice but to.
It had happened.
Nux was... dead.
And... he wasn’t coming back.
Thud
Felberta, who had been strong till the last moment, fell on her knees with a hollow look on her face once the reality sunk in.
This time however, no one came to support her.
Because the rest of the women were the same.
Amaya was prepared to kill herself right now and reunite with Nux but—
Do not curse them with the life of an orphan because of my mistake.

Nux’s words echoed in her mind and Orion’s face appeared inside her head, she sensed their connection and her gaze fell on Orion, who was passed out in his room, oblivious to everything that was happening.
And for a moment—
Amaya just stared at her child.
The last mark of Nux’s presence, the proof of her and Nux’s love...
She...
Even she, who hadn’t seen anything beyond Nux her entire life, couldn’t leave Orion alone. She didn’t have the heart to do it.
Please live on.
Nux’s request rang in her head again and...
Thud
Amaya too, helplessly fell on her knees with a hollow look on her face.
"When..."

Shadow on the other hand, was thinking of something else. She could feel it, the absolute control she had over the Universe now. It was far, far stronger than the control she had when Nux was inside the Temple of Time.
But...
How...?
She was always the Goddess of the Universe, but she wasn’t the creator, neither was she a being who supported the Universe’s very existence.
While she could temporarily control the Universe, the Universe itself was still Nux.
That would never change.
Then...
How did it change?
When did it change?
Shadow thought about it and—
Her expression changed when she realized when it happened.
That moment when she woke up after a month feeling... strange but better than before... (Chapter 2247)
That was when Nux did it—
Hundreds of years ago...
Did he... plan all of it in advance...?
Shadow wondered in her head, but she shook her head.
Nux would never actively plan this.
He just...
Shadow couldn’t come up with an explanation, she just placed her hand on her chest, closed her eyes and once again—
Silence took over Nux’s Universe as the women... lost themselves.

chapters.title: Chapter 2365: The End.
paragraphs: "So do all of us a favor and...
Get rid of him.
Now."
The Seer spoke as she looked at Nux.
Nux looked back at her with the same unconcealed rage, he tried to move, to tear this woman apart but the Seer just smiled gently.
"Don’t try it, Nux.
Your tricks do not work on me, you should know that by now."
Then, she glanced at Zylarith and the other Infinities and—
"When I say get rid of him—
I do not mean kill him.
Killing him is not enough, he is not a being of our Universe, if you kill him, his Soul would simply return to his own Universe, whichhecontrols, allowing him to return from death."
"Then... what do we do...?"
Ul’Thakar questioned with a frown. At that question, the Seer looked at Nux and—
"Erase his existence."
She declared.
"Remove his Soul from every single timeline, forcefully tear his connection with his Universe, his World, or any other entity.
Erase him in a way the Multiverse forgets about him.
Permanently."
The Seer answered and hearing those words—
Nux’s expression changed.
The rage in his eyes was replaced with... hopelessness.
That was his last card.
He wanted the Infinities to kill him in a hurry so he could revive using Lane’s Law back in his own Universe.
This was also the reason he had been glaring at the Seer all this while, to divert her mind from his immortality, to fool her just this once—
But she saw right through him and—
It truly was over.
And the moment Nux realized it—
He closed his eyes and...
He gave his Universe to Shadow and cut whatever connection he had with his Universe, his wives, and his children.
Yes.
Nux Leander surrendered.
When the Seer saw it, a small, untraceable smile appeared on her face.
"But if we do that, even we wouldn’t be able to recover his body, his memories and the secrets he hides."
Zylarith spoke with a frown.
The Seer looked at him and—
"If his secrets are more important to you than your life then..."
She didn’t need to complete that sentence.
The Five Infinities were greedy, they wanted to absorb everything Nux had to offer, they wanted to learn his secrets, they wanted to know what sort of existence Nux Leander was but—
Did any of it matter more than their lives?
This was a being who had fought Five Infinities alone and nearly won, that too, when he was barely a few thousand years old.
If this being somehow escaped—
None of them knew what would happen.
"She is right."
Orravyn moved first, his relics slowly turning towards Nux.
"We need to ensure he doesn’t see the next hour.
No matter the cost."
Hearing those words, Nux, who had broken his connection with his wives, his children, his Universe and had nothing more to lose—
He raised his head and looked at the so-called Five Strongest Beings standing in front of him, then—
He grinned.
"You sound... afraid."
He taunted, one last time.
"You should be silent."
Ul’Thakar dismissed him, Darkness moved around him threateningly.
But all the pretentious fear in Nux’s eyes disappeared, he no longer cared.
"You needed... five."
His grin widened.
Ul’Thakar’s claws tightened at those words but—
"Do not let him provoke you."
Seraphielle spoke up as the Light around her moved, not towards Nux, but outside, towards time, memories, towards... every place where Nux’s existence had left a mark.
Equarios raised one hand.
A vast scale appeared above Nux.
On one side of the scale was Nux, on the other side was everything connected to him.
His body.
His Soul.
His Universe.
His wives.
His people.
His worlds.
His past.
His future.
His name.
His victories.
His wounds.
His bonds.
His every possible return.
"I will separate him from everything that can call him back."
Equarios declared as he stared at his scale, he didn’t know Nux had already broken most of those connections. Not that he cared.
"Begin."
The Five Infinities moved together like executioners.
Orravyn’s Archive moved and every record of Nux Leander’s existence that he had recorded till now appeared in the Archive pages.
And then—
Those pages burned.
Nux’s name, his presence, his existence, his impact, even the memories other people had of him.
It all started to disappear.
"Cowards.
That is what you are all."
Nux raised his voice, his eyes glaring at the enemies with absolute rage.
"I told you to be silent."
Ul’Thakar snarled.
Then, Seraphielle’s Light moved.
Her Law of Absolute Light carried the erasure forward, from other timelines, the timelines Nux may and may not have affected.
She started erasing him from those timelines.
Then, it was Ul’Thakar’s turn.
If the Law of Absolute Light removed the marks that could be seen, the Law of Absolute Darkness started devouring what remained... unseen.
He opened his mouth and the darkness that came from him swallowed shadows of Nux’s records, his leftover traces, his echoes that might have remained after Light burned the surface.
Ul’Thakar swallowed it all.
That was when Zylarith grinned as he glanced at Nux and his enraged expression.
"Still no trace of fear, huh?"
He chuckled.
"Fear?"
Nux grinned.
"I think we all know who here is actually moving out of fear, don’t we?"
Nux tried to talk, to taunt.
10 more seconds.
That was all he needed.
10 more seconds.
But—
"Stubborn to the very end."
Zylarith laughed, then, he shook his head and—
"Well, you are stubborn because you still mean something.
Let me help you with that."
He spoke and the Chaos moved and—
Nux’s existence began to contradict itself, the very meaning of his existence was now being erased.
And—
"Now."
Orravyn declared and all five Infinities poured their power into the execution and—
Nux’s body began to... disappear.
His fingers, his hands, his arms, his chest, his heart, his neck, his face...
Only his eyes remained for a moment.
The golden shine in them was still intense, his eyes were still burning with rage, hatred and unwillingness.
At the very end—
Those eyes looked at the Seer.
The Seer looked back at them.
And for the first time, there was no smile on her face.
Nux’s eyes seemed to say something, but his mouth was gone, no words came out, in the end—
Even his eyes disappeared and—
Absolute silence fell all over the Void.
Nux Leander was gone.

Now."
The Seer spoke as she looked at Nux.

Permanently."

None of them knew what would happen.

Orravyn moved first, his relics slowly turning towards Nux.
