chapters.title: Chapter 2366: How am I... still sensing it...?
paragraphs: After being erased, Nux opened his eyes, or at least he thought he did, but nothing around him changed.
There was only Darkness around him, Darkness he wasn’t familiar with, Darkness that was more overwhelming than even Ul’Thakar’s Darkness.
A Darkness with no... meaning.
Nux tried to look around, to expand his senses, to understand where he was—
But nothing worked.
Let alone being able to understand where he was—
He couldn’t even feel his own self.
He could not feel his body.
He could not feel his heart beating inside his chest.
He could not breathe.
He could not blink.
He could not even tell if he still had eyes.
He was... just there.
Then, slowly, a thought appeared in his mind.
’So this is it?’
He tried to sense his connection again but as he expected—
There was nothing.
His Primordial Laws.
His Universe.
His... wives.
It was... completely empty.
’Is this what it means... to be erased...?’
He thought to himself.
’Is this where erased beings go?’
More questions appeared in his head.
’What is this place? Or is this not even aplaceto begin with?’
The more he thought about it, the stranger it became.
’If I was truly erased, then how am I still thinking?
If I no longer have a Soul then—
Why am I still conscious?
Was this...
Thelast piece of me?
Or is my mind taking longer to disappear?’
That could definitely be a possibility.
So Nux waited for something to happen.
Who knows?
He might meet a beautiful goddess who would reincarnate him into a world of beautiful vampires, dragons, cat gir—
’That has already happened to me, huh?’
He laughed at his own joke.
’How does this thing work? Do erased Souls get reincarnated too? But then what would be the point of erasing them?’
At this point, Nux knew a lot about the Universe, or even the Multiverse. Reincarnation was common knowledge to him.
What he and almost any being in the Universe did not know about was... erasure.
What happens after one is erased?
People believed they just... disappear.
End of the story.
But here he was—
Still conscious.
Somewhere he didn’t know.
’Hmm, maybe this is how it ends.’
Another theory came to his mind.
’Maybe it wears the mind down first.’
That made more sense.
A place where one could not move, could not feel, see, hear, touch... anything, even the strongest mind would eventually begin to... rot.
First, the concept of colors would fade, then names would lose meaning, emotions would grow dull, theselfwould blur and then...
The last piece of consciousness would become numb to... nothingness.
’So that’s the plan?’
If he had a mouth, he would have chuckled.
’Make me numb?
You are welcome to try.’
He thought to himself.
He could exist with the memories of his wives for Eternity.
He would not allow himself to fade away.
So with that thought in his mind, he took the challenge.
To not... lose himself in this darkness.
To... not be erased.
Time passed.
If the concept of time even existed here in the first place.
Then suddenly, while Nux was still trying to keep his mind intact—
Something happened.
A small, extremely faint connection that he wouldn’t even have felt if he had given up and accepted his fate.
Nux focused on it instantly, for the first time since he had opened his eyes in this darkness, he could manage to sense something other than himself, so he needed to know what it was.
Nux reached for the connection and unlike others, this connection answered.
And the moment it did, the moment he recognized it—
If Nux had a face, it would have turned cold.
It was the Bloodedge.
His—no, the Seer’s Sword.
Nux’s anger flared. He cursed himself for not breaking this connection at that very moment, but very soon, he recalled that he didn’t exactly have the time to do it.
Not when he was surrounded by the five strongest beings in the Universe.
But just as Nux thought about it, another thought appeared in his head—
’How am I... still sensing it...?’
He wondered.
His connection with all his weapons was broken when the Infinities erased him, then...
How was he still feeling the connection...?
And why just the Bloodedge?
Nux focused harder.
That was when he sensed it—
Something else that was connected to the Bloodedge.
A... Path.
An... opening.
He couldn’t see it, there was still Darkness all around him,
But he couldfeelit.
A way out of this place.
That alone was enough.
Nux reached toward the opening but—
Nothing happened.
He tried to move towards the opening, to use the connection and pull himself towards it, to use the Bloodedge to make the path but—
No matter what he did—
Nothing happened.
Nux did not have a body, nor a soul, he had no Laws, no powers, he didn’t even actually exist—
He was... merely a fragment of thoughts, the last remaining Will that was supposed to fade away.
And anything that did not have any form of body, be it a physical body or a Soul—
It was not supposed to move.
It was... impossible.
’Heh.’
Nux smiled at that.
’Impossible, huh...’
He collected himself.
He tried to sense it, his Law of Anomaly, the Power that made even the Impossible Possible but—
He couldn’t do it.
Even the Law of Anomaly did not exist here.
Nothingcouldexist here.
That too... was impossible.
But Nux did not care.
His mind, or whatever was left of it, started working, it started thinking.
In the battle against the Five Infinities, he was still restricted by time, most of his attention was on the battle so he couldn’t exactly focus either—
But now—
Now it was different.
Now he had all the time and attention in the world, now—
He could deepen his understanding even further.
So Nux made a decision.
This was not where he was going to fall.
No.
He was going to gather his thoughts, he was going to understand his own powers, and once again—
He was going to make the Impossible Possible.

chapters.title: Chapter 2367: The Multiverse.
paragraphs: Nux remained in whatever state he was in for he didn’t know how long. He had already sorted Zylarith’s distorted memories in his head before he died, and now, he had watched and comprehended it all.
His understanding of the Law of Absolute Chaos was at the Level of an Infinity.
And the best part?
At this point, theQuality of Energydidn’t even matter.
After all, he now had the power to affect reality itself with his power. He could replace the Universe’s Chaos withhisChaos, no matter whether he was in his own Universe, or any other.
Of course, against a being like Zylarith, it would still be difficult since the Quality of Energy would be lacking compared to his but against other Infinities?
He would be no different than Zylarith.
In fact, he would be much stronger than Zylarith because of his other abilities and his physical body.
Not that... any of it mattered right now...
Because—
Even with Zylarith’s memories, even with the Law of Absolute Chaos, even when he had quite a few answers to questions he had been wondering about for a long time—
It did not matter because—
His understanding of Impossibility did not increase.
Well, it did increase, if he was in his Universe or even in the Main Universe, he would have been able to use the Power of Anomaly more accurately, with much less Energy.
It might even have been enough to actually defeat the Five Infinities.
But—
In here, it didn’t change anything.
The Law of Absolute Chaos, the Law that Nux had based his Law of Anomaly on needed Energy.
The Law of Anomaly needed... Energy.
All this time, Nux had almost infinite Energy, so he never once cared about it, but in here—
The concept of Energy did not exist.
So the Law of Anomaly couldn’t be used either.
Or at least...
ThecurrentLaw of Anomaly couldn’t be used.
Yes, even now, Nux hadn’t given up.
He simply... scratched away the restriction he set upon himself and his Law.
The Law of Anomaly allowed him to be out of theSystem, and the very fact that Laws needed Energy to be usedwaspartofthe System.
He was trying to leave the System while still thinking under its restrictions.
So...
That was what Nux did.
He completely abandoned the System.
He scratched the approach he initially picked, Zylarith’s memory, his Chaos, he no longer needed it to grow his understanding of Impossibility.
After all, Chaos and Anomaly were two different powers.
Trying to comprehend Anomaly by using Chaos as the thread would only take him so far—
Now, he needed to focus entirely on Anomaly and that was exactly what he did.
And...
He did it for hours, days, months, years, decades, centuries, even Eons maybe—
He didn’t know, neither did it matter because the concept of time did not exist here.
Nux simply sat there, developed his understanding of Anomaly and finally—
He moved.
In a state where moving should not be possible—
He moved.
And he passed through that opening he sensed through the Bloodedge.
The next moment—
An endless amount of Light struck him from all sides. For a moment, he couldn’t see but after he got used to the blinding light and was finally able to look around—
He saw it.
The space around him was dark, but not like the darkness he had escaped from. This darkness was deep and full. Inside it, countless streams of light stretched in every direction.
It was... vast.
Nux didn’t even have a name for what it was or what it looked like.
Rivers? Roots? Veins?
They all matched but... a clearer description would be...
Streams of multi-coloured lightning frozen in the middle of a storm, just... a few hundred thousand times grander.
These massive glowing branches spread through the void, twisting and turning and splitting again and again until even the smallest thread carried more worlds than Nux could count.
Some branches were white-blue, bright and cold like newborn stars.
Some were gold, thick and ancient, moving slowly as if their history was too heavy.
Some were violet and pink, beautiful but unstable, shaking as if they were still deciding what shape they wanted to take.
Some were crimson, wild and violent, full of war, fire, and blood.
Some were silver, quiet and smooth, almost too perfect.
Some were dark, nearly black, where death and destruction ruled above all.
*Picture*
"What the hell is this...?"
Nux wondered out loud, the fact that he managed to speak confused him as well. He looked down and he realized he had a body of his own.
Well, not a body in a complete sense, he didn’t have a Physical Body, neither was it a Complete Soul.
It was... just scattered fragments of his thoughts that were given a shape in this place.
That in itself was something Nux couldn’t explain.
But right now—
His mind was too overwhelmed by the grand majesty of this place he was in to even think about his body, his soul, or whatever shape he was in.
He wanted to know.
He wanted to understand what this place was.
He wanted answers.
And—
"It’s the Multiverse."
He got the answer he was looking for.
Nux frowned.
There was someone here other than him?
He turned around and then—
His eyes fell on her.

A woman wearing a black hooded robe that seemed like it was made from literal stars. Beautiful golden patterns were designed on the robe, glowing softly, then fading and appearing again in different places.
And her face—
It was beautiful.
Ridiculously beautiful, almost... perfect in a way. She had pale skin, full lips but her eyes...
Her eyes were covered with a dark veil.
And the moment he saw her, Nux’s body trembled with unconcealed, uncontrollable rage.
He glared at the woman who betrayed him.
Yes.
The woman in front of him was none other than the Seer.
And seeing him glaring at her like that—
The woman smiled—
"It is a pleasure to finally meet you, Nux Leander."

They all matched but... a clearer description would be...
Streams of multi-coloured lightning frozen in the middle of a storm, just... a few hundred thousand times grander.
These massive glowing branches spread through the void, twisting and turning and splitting again and again until even the smallest thread carried more worlds than Nux could count.
Some branches were white-blue, bright and cold like newborn stars.
Some were gold, thick and ancient, moving slowly as if their history was too heavy.
Some were violet and pink, beautiful but unstable, shaking as if they were still deciding what shape they wanted to take.
Some were crimson, wild and violent, full of war, fire, and blood.
Some were silver, quiet and smooth, almost too perfect.
Some were dark, nearly black, where death and destruction ruled above all.
*Picture*
"What the hell is this...?"
Nux wondered out loud, the fact that he managed to speak confused him as well.
He looked down and he realized he had a body of his own.
Well, not a body in a complete sense, he didn’t have a Physical Body, neither was it a Complete Soul.
It was... just scattered fragments of his thoughts that were given a shape in this place.
That in itself was something Nux couldn’t explain.
But right now—
His mind was too overwhelmed by the grand majesty of this place he was in to even think about his body, his soul, or whatever shape he was in.
He wanted to know.
He wanted to understand what this place was.
He wanted answers.
And—
"It’s the Multiverse."
He got the answer he was looking for.
Nux frowned.
There was someone here other than him?
He turned around and then—
His eyes fell on her.
A woman wearing a black hooded robe that seemed like it was made from literal stars.
Beautiful golden patterns were designed on the robe, glowing softly, then fading and appearing again in different places.
And her face—
It was beautiful.
Ridiculously beautiful, almost... perfect in a way.
She had pale skin, full lips but her eyes...
Her eyes were covered with a dark veil.
And the moment he saw her, Nux’s body trembled with unconcealed, uncontrollable rage.
He glared at the woman who betrayed him.
Yes.
The woman in front of him was none other than the Seer.
And seeing him glaring at her like that—
The woman smiled—
"It is a pleasure to finally meet you, Nux Leander."

chapters.title: Chapter 2368: I promised you Three Gifts.
paragraphs: "It is a pleasure to finally meet you, Nux Leander."
The woman smiled.
Her words made Nux frown.
Finally...?
The Seer looked at his face and chuckled—
"I thought you would attack me the moment you saw me."
"I cannot hurt you in this form."
Nux answered honestly.
The moment he saw her—
It was his first thought.
To tear her apart and rip her into pieces, to make her scream, to make her suffer agony she had never experienced in her entire life, to make her regret ever being born but—
The moment he tried to move, to gather any form of Energy at all—
He couldn’t do it.
He was... powerless here.
Not to mention...
The woman standing in front of him...
While she indeed looked like the Seer he always knew, something about her was... different. She was... fuller.
Or...
More complete.
Not to mention the wordfinallywas still stuck in his head.
"Your self-control is surprisingly admirable. I’ve always believed you lacked in that area."
The Seer commented like she was making an observation. Nux didn’t care about her comment, instead—
"What are you doing here?"
He asked directly and the instant he did, her smile widened, almost as if she was waiting for him to ask this.
"Did you forget?
I promised you Three Gifts.
The Third is still pending."
"My... gift...?"
Nux blinked.
Was this woman... rubbing it in?
It didn’t seem like it.
"You already gave me that."
He spoke in a tone much colder than before.
"No, I never said that was my third gift."
The Seer just smiled.
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"You said you came to give me my third gift, a gift that would show me a way out of the situation I was in."
Nux repeated what the Seer had said that day, word for word.
It wasn’t a conversation he could forget—not when he replayed it in his head countless times and bitterly laughed at himself for being made a fool of.
His expression became even colder when he thought about it.
The Seer, on the other hand, just shrugged—
"I said I came to give you the third gift, I never saidthatwas my gift."
"What are you trying to say?"
Nux asked directly, he had no heart for wordplay right now.
The Seer understood that, so she answered honestly—
"I am here to give you the gift I promised."
"You already betrayed me once, what makes you believe I will trust you again?"
Nux asked coldly, but the Seer—
"Do you have any other choice?"
And Nux turned silent.
He looked around, at the random place he was in, he tried to sense his connections, but again, nothing existed.
He couldn’t sense his wives, he couldn’t tell whether they were alive or not, nothing, he couldn’t do anything right now.
And that made him feel... pathetic.
He looked at the Seer with cold hatred and—
"So you are essentially forcing me to take your gift."
He laughed dryly, there wasn’t a hint of amusement on his face.
And that was when the Seer’s face turned solemn—
"Stop looking at me like that, Nux Leander."
Then, she took a step towards Nux and—
"I never once lied to you."
"You betrayed me."
"I did what was necessary."
The Seer explained herself and Nux—
"Necessary?"
He raised his eyebrow.
"You had me killed, you had me separated from my wives and my children, and now you come here talking about some ridiculous gift like nothing happened, saying all you did was necessary!?
Woman, do not think I cannot kill you just because of the state I am in."
Nux spoke, his eyes flaring with anger he could no longer control.
"I may not be able to kill you right now, but the longer you stay here, the stronger my hatred will be, and Iwillfind a way to kill you."
He spoke in an overwhelming tone that would make most beings shiver in fright.
But not the Seer.
She stared at Nux with the same expression and—
"I told you before, my gift would be something you absolutely nee—"

"There is nothing I need from you anymore. I was winning, I would have won if it weren’t for your Sword betraying me at the last second, I could have defeated Zylarith, I could have absorbed him, I could have become stronger, I could have then defeated the Four Infinities, all while my wives would have been near m—"
Nux tried to cut her off but—
"Listen to me."
The Seer raised her voice and for some reason—
Nux did stop.
And when the Seer finally had his attention, she began—
"From the beginning, I have always been clear.
I never said I would be giving you these gifts for free, I said I need something from you in return.
And you winning against those five and becoming the God of the Main Universe would not give me what I want."
Nux remained silent.
His mind, however, couldn’t stop thinking.
Even being a Universe’s God wouldn’t be able to give her what she wanted...?
But if he thought about it—
The Seer was a being who knew almost everything about the Universe, she was the only being who knew the truth about him, something that even the Infinities did not know.
Who knew what else she could have known?
Honestly, if she wanted, she could have supported just any one of the Infinities if what she wanted could be given to her by a Universe’s God.
Then...
"What is it that you want?"
Nux questioned.
The Seer looked at him for a moment, then, she shook her head.
"Let’s leave that aside for no—"
"That will not do."
Nux interrupted her again.
"You either tell me what you want, or don’t bother talking."
He was sick.
He had no energy, nor the patience left to deal with her shenanigans. If this was going to happen, it would happen on his terms.
But the Seer—
"Nux."
She called out with a solemn, convincing look on her face and—
"I will not hurt you, your wives, or your children in any way.
I promise you that."
"Woman, I am dead."

chapters.title: Chapter 2369: Aren’t you supposed to know everything?
paragraphs: "I will not hurt you, your wives, or your children in any way.
I promise you that."
The Seer spoke with a convincing look on her face.
"Woman, if it hasn’t sunk in yet, I am dead.
I do not think youcanhurt me even if you wanted to."
"So are you just going to let death stop you?"
The Seer questioned and Nux looked at her with a deadpan look on his face.
Just... what was wrong with this woman?
"I have no desire to help you, I have no desire for whatever you have for me."
Nux spoke as he decided to leave.
He changed his mind, that empty darkness was far better than being in her presence.
But before he could leave—
"And what if what I have is a way for you to return to your wives?"
Nux paused.
The Seer smiled knowingly, Nux noticed that smile and this time, he had no plans to believe her.
"I no longer trust you."
"Good thing I was willing to give your Gift first and then ask for the favor in return, no?"
The Seer shrugged and Nux...
He just narrowed his eyes even further.
"...you do realize you are the reason I am separated from my wives in the first place, correct?"
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"You realize I hate you to the very core of my being, correct?"
"As much as it hurts me, I know that, yes."
She nodded again.
"Then what makes you believe I will help you after I get what I want?"
"Because we gave each other our words, I followed through with mine, I know you will follow through with yours."
The Seer answered and Nux just laughed out loud.
"You have misjudged me.
I do not put much weight on my words, not when it doesn’t benefit me."
"I made a prediction after having observed you for longer than you think, Nux. I may be wrong and if I am then I would just assume I made a foolish mistake.
It is not like I have any other choice.
You are the only Entity in the Multiverse who can give me what I want."
The Seer answered honestly, showing vulnerability for the first time ever since she met Nux. Nux looked at her, for a moment, he wanted to go, to not fall for her words again but...
The gift she offered was simply too valuable to refuse.
Not to mention...
He didn’t exactly have a lot to lose at this point.
So...
"What is your gift?"
He asked.
The Seer’s smile widened, she looked genuinely pleased, as if Nux agreeing to her request wasn’t something she was absolutely certain about like she usually was with such things.
Then, she extended her hands to the side, like she was presenting it to him and Nux... he raised his eyebrows.
"You are giving me... the Multiverse...?"
The Seer chuckled at the dubiousness of that statement.
"If I could, I would.
I, unfortunately, do not have that authority."
She shook her head.
Then, she looked around and—
"You being able to stand here is my gift to you."
"What does that mean?"
Nux questioned with a frown on his face.
"Look around you, Nux.
How many more beings do you see here?"
She asked a simple question.
Nux frowned, then, as if he hadn’t given it a thought all this while, he looked around, expanded his senses to however far he could and...
He didn’t sense a single other soul here.
"This is the Multiverse.
The Root of existence itself.
No living Entity is supposed to be here."
"Then how am I..."
Nux didn’t understand, the Seer on the other hand, just chuckled and—
"Do you think you are a living entity now?"
"What...?"
Nux’s frown deepened, then, he thought about what she said for a moment and his expression changed.
"So that’s why..."
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"No being with a Physical Body, a Soul, or any connection to any Universe, can exist in the Multiverse.
This is why I arranged for you to fight against the Infinities.
So they could defeat you and send you here."
The Seer revealed, then, at the end, she passed another comment.
"Though you made it much harder for me than it had to be."
"Hah?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.
The Seer just sighed.
"I never intended to appear at the very last second, you know?
I honestly never even expected you to put up that much of a fight, not to mention nearly win if I hadn’t appeared."
"So you just wanted me to go down without a fight?"
"Without a fight? You were battling Five Infinities, I expected a fight, but not for you to get into a position of outright defeating them!
I doubted if you could even defeat Zylarith in your own Universe!
But I took that gamble because I believed you had the power to end the battle anytime you wanted, so at the very least, you wouldn’t die."
"You still gave me Bloodedge..."
Nux blamed, still doubting her words.
"Of course I did, I didn’t want you to win."
"What if I hadn’t won against Zylarith and ended the battle instead?"
Nux asked with a curious look on his face.
"Then I would have waited until you were stronger than you are right now and would have made you two fight again."
"Until I am strong enough to defeat him, then once I use the Bloodedge, it would create an opening, allowing the Infinities to force their way in and I am surrounded—
Just like it happened."
Nux completed and the Seer nodded.
"That is correct."
Nux blinked at the shamelessness. Then, he frowned again—
"Aren’t you supposed to know everything?
Why did you plan so thoroughly?
You must have known how everything was supposed to play out from the very beginning, no?"
He asked curiously.
All this while, he was under the impression that the Seer was from the Future or someone whocouldsee the Future.
But...
If one indeed was from the Future, then shouldn’t she be far more certain of her plan than this?
That was when the Seer revealed the truth—
"I could never see your Future, Nux.
Because your Future wasn’t written."

chapters.title: Chapter 2370: Then there is you.
paragraphs: "I could never see your Future, Nux.
Because your Future wasn’t written."
The Seer revealed the truth and Nux’s expression changed.
"You... could never see the Future...?"
"I could and still can see the Future.
I just could never seeyourfuture.
There is a difference."
Nux’s frown deepened.
He asked in confusion.
The Seer stayed silent for a small while, then, she turned towards the vast Multiverse in front of her.
"You see this?"
Nux turned towards the Multiverse and for a moment, he remained silent.
This place was... beautiful.
And majestic.
He didn’t even dare compare his own Universe to it, but even when he compared the Main Universe, a fully grown Universe, it felt... insignificant.
For the first time in a long, long while, Nux felt... small.
"You see that branch?"

The Seer then pointed at a particular branch near the very edge, it wasn’t the biggest branch there, neither was it the strongest, just an average branch, in the middle of trillions of other branches.
"That’s what you call the Main Universe."
The Seer revealed and Nux’s eyes widened in surprise.
"That’s... the Main Universe...?
Just that...?"
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"That little branch depicts the start to the end of the Main Universe, everything that has happened, everything that is happening, everything that is supposed to happen, it is all in there.
That is about one hundred quindecillion years."
"That little branch is... one hundred quindecillion years...?"
Nux blinked.
That was 10^47 years.
"Well..."
The Seer was now hesitating.
"It is somewhere around that number, could be bigger or smaller."
Nux nodded in understanding.
"Makes sense, there is no way to know the accurate number. There must always be variations."
But again, the Seer shook her head.
"No, that is not true."
Then, she pointed at another branch right next to their Universe and—
"Take that Universe for example.
That branch starts from its beginning to its end.

That is exactly seventy-three quindecillion, eight hundred forty-six quattuordecillion, two hundred ninety-one tredecillion, five hundred eight duodecillion, four hundred seventy-two undecillion, nine hundred thirty-six decillion years."
Nux simply blinked at those words.
"Just... what are you talking about..."
The absurd numbers didn’t confuse him, his mind was far more developed than to be confused by mere numbers, but what the Seer was saying was still overwhelming.
"How do you have the exact numbers for that Universe, but not the Main Universe?"
He asked with an innocent look on his face and the Seer—
She just looked at him and did not say anything.
Nux’s frown deepened even more, but then, as he noticed that the Seer wasn’t saying anything else—
He finally realized it—
"It’s me, isn’t it?"
And the Seer smiled.
"That is correct."
That was when she pointed towards another branch far, far away, a branch Nux noticed was different from the rest the moment his eyes fell on it.
The first thing he noticed was how... small that branch was.
It was so small that it looked like a dot instead of a branch but that wasn’t the strange part, there were countless branches like this in this place.
What made this one stand out was because... this branch wasn’t particularly a... branch.
Every other branch here, every single Universe in this place was connected to at least one other branch.
But this particular one was different.
It was independent.
It wasn’t connected to any other branch, it was just... there.
Out of nowhere, almost as if one day, it just rudely appeared out of nowhere.
’Would this one be called the stuck-up sibling in the family of the Multiverse, the Universe that no one likes?’
Nux wondered in his head and just then—
"That’s you."
The Seer revealed.
And Nux’s expression changed.
"...what?"
"That is your Universe."
The instant he heard those words, Nux finally understood.
The Seer smiled at that, then, she started explaining, just to ensure they were on the same page.
"At the beginning of existence—
There was no difference between a Universe and a Multiverse.
There was only one thing.
A Single Root, a Root with no branches, no alternate paths, no separate realities.
It was the first and only existence. The true Main Universe.
But as that Universe grew, the beings inside it began to understand Time. Then, eventually—
They began to touch it.

Some looked into the future, some returned to the past, some changed moments that were never meant to change, and every time the Power of Time was used deeply enough to disturb the pre-decided future of that Universe—
ABranchwas born.
At first, those Branches were fragile. They were only possible futures, thin streams of reality still connected to the Single Root, some of them couldn’t support themselves and decayed on their own.
But some...
Some continued to grow.
They stabilized, they formed their own histories, their own worlds, their own Laws, their own... Wills.
And once a Branch grew strong enough, it no longer remained aBranch.
It became a fully independent Universe.
A newMain Universe.
Then that new Main Universe gave birth to new beings who also discovered Time and they too interfered with it, they too changed what should not have been, and from them—
More Branches were born.
Those Branches then became more Universes.
Those Universes created more Branches, and those Branches created more Universes.
This continued for countless Multiversal Aeons until eventually—
The Single Root, which was once alone in the endless dark—
Became aforest of realities.
A living structure of light, Time, fate, and consequences."
"The Multiverse."
Nux completed the sentence.
"Yes."

"Then there is you."
She spoke and Nux...
He had no idea what he was supposed to say here.
He...
He really was the odd one out in the family, huh...

I just could never seeyourfuture.

Nux’s frown deepened.
He asked in confusion.

"You see this?"
Nux turned towards the Multiverse and for a moment, he remained silent.

And majestic.

For the first time in a long, long while, Nux felt... small.
"You see that branch?"

The Seer then pointed at a particular branch near the very edge, it wasn’t the biggest branch there, neither was it the strongest, just an average branch, in the middle of trillions of other branches.
"That’s what you call the Main Universe."
The Seer revealed and Nux’s eyes widened in surprise.
"That’s... the Main Universe...?
Just that...?"
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"That little branch depicts the start to the end of the Main Universe, everything that has happened, everything that is happening, everything that is supposed to happen, it is all in there.

"That little branch is... one hundred quindecillion years...?"
Nux blinked.
That was 10^47 years.
"Well..."
The Seer was now hesitating.
"It is somewhere around that number, could be bigger or smaller."
Nux nodded in understanding.
"Makes sense, there is no way to know the accurate number.

"No, that is not true."

chapters.title: Chapter 2371: You corrupted that Universe’s Future with your presence.
paragraphs: "A Family of Universes where every single Universe is connected to at least one other Universe.
A Family of Universes where every single Universe has its own unique ’Time’ that is still, in some way, connected to the Universe it originated from."
The Seer then turned back towards Nux and—
"Then there is you.
An entirely independent Universe with a completely different concept of time that I cannot comprehend."
"What do you mean when you say you cannot comprehend...?"
Nux asked with a light frown on his face.
The Seer turned back to the Multiverse and began—
"Every single Universe you see here, I have the ability to see its end, its present, and its future.
Even the Universes that do not seem complete right now, Universes that you see are still growing right now—
I can visit them and I can see their past, present, and the future that is yet to be formed."
Nux widened his eyes in shock.
Being able to see the Past, Present and the Future of every single Universe in the Multiverse?
What’s with that absurd ability?
How does it even make any sense?
Just... how much information is stored in her head...?
He couldn’t help but wonder all that in his head, but the Seer just chuckled, then, she looked at the branch that represented Nux’s Universe, then at him—
"Every Universe, but Yours."
She completed and Nux realized the reason.
"Because Time in my Universe does not follow the General Concept of Time the other Universes here follow."
The Seer shrugged and answered honestly.
"I do not know the reason.
You are the said Universe, so maybe what you are saying is correct.
I only know I am unable to see yours or your Universe’s future."
Nux nodded.
He was pretty much certain that he was correct.

The Time in his Universe was anchored to Emotions, that concept in itself was entirely different than the Concept of Time the rest of the Universes follow, this was the reason the Seer couldn’t look into his Universe or him.
And as he thought about it—
Nux finally had the answer to his initial question.
"So the reason you are not certain when it comes to the Main Universe’s numbers..."
The Seer nodded at those words—
"That is correct.
Ever since you became an Independent Universe, the Main Universe’s Future, which is majorly affected by your presence, has become uncertain too."
"So it is not like you cannot look into it, it is just... the ’Future’ doesn’t even exist."
Nux tried to put it in words.
The Seer chuckled at the simplification.
"Or in other words, you corrupted that Universe’s Future with your presence."
"No wonder the Universe screamed every time I did something huh..."
The Seer laughed at those words.
A small smile appeared on Nux’s face as well.
For a moment, none of them said anything, Nux just stared at the Seer and after a while—
"Ask what you want to ask, Nux."
The Seer commented, as if she read his mind and that made Nux frown.
"If you cannot see the future, how do you know what I am thinking? Because I am certain you cannot read my mind."
"You are correct, I cannot read your mind."
The Seer admitted.
"Then how?"
Nux asked.
The Seer smiled lightly and—
"I told you before, did I not?
I’ve observed you, longer than you realize it."
She commented, looking right into his eyes.
"What does that mean?"
Nux tilted his head in curiosity.
"It is exactly what I mean, Nux Leander.
I’ve observed you, from the very beginning, when you were a child in an entirely different Universe, in the World they called Earth.
I’ve been watching you since then.
And not just you—
I’ve watched every single version of you in the Multiverse.
A version where you died a quick death.
A version where you lost a battle you won in this life.
A version where you had more wives than you do now.
A version where you had no wives at all.
A version where you were a heartless being with no limits.
A version where you sacrificed yourself for the greater good.
I’ve watched quindecillions of you, Nux Leander.
I understand you more than you can think—
I understand you... more than your own wives do."
The Seer took a small pause, looking at the smallest of Nux’s reactions.
"And that is what allows me to take an educated guess as to what you have done, what you are going to do, and what you are thinking of doing.
A guess that is almost never wrong."
"That sounds... complicated."
Nux commented, slightly overwhelmed by the woman standing in front of him.
"When you do it enough times, it becomes quite simple."
The Seer just chuckled.
Nux looked at her, then he thought about what she just said...
"Quindecillions of me huh..."
He commented.
"So many...meexist in the Multiverse, huh."
"Used to exist."
The Seer corrected.
"...what?"
Nux’s expression changed.
"So many of you... used to exist in the Universe. Not anymore."
"Not anymore...?"
Nux’s frown deepened and the Seer looked at him as if it couldn’t be more obvious and—
"You are an Anomaly, Nux.
And no, I do not say that because that is what those in that little Universe call you.
I say it because youarean Anomaly.
A Multiversal Anomaly.
A... mistake.
An entity that should not exist."
Nux stared at her in silence, the Seer, however, didn’t stop.
"So that is what the Multiverse did.
It erased you and every being connected to you, acting like you and your Universe simply do not exist."
"I was... erased...? By the Multiverse...?"
Nux blinked.
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"Every other Universe other than the one you call the Main Universe has no record of you either, this was the second reason I told the Infinities to erase you when they killed you.
That way—
That Universe wouldn’t have any record of you either—
This is also the reason what you are seeing right now is a much more stabilized version of that Universe.
When you were alive—
It was... far worse."
At those words, Nux looked at the Seer, then he looked at the ’Main Universe’ and...
"...right."
No other word came out of his mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 2372: Who killed you?
paragraphs: "...right."
No other word came out of Nux’s mouth. Everything the Seer said made sense in his head, he was just... overwhelmed by the absurdity of it all.
"So what you are saying is...
Before I came to this Universe, it was normal like every other Universe, I disrupted it all, but now that I am gone, it is stabilizing again, correct?"
He asked, trying to see if he understood everything properly or not.
"No, your arrival did not disrupt the Universe’s Timeline."
The Seer shook her head.

"You weresupposedto arrive in this Universe. It may be a rare occurrence, but there have been instances where different Universes in the Multiverse interact with each other for a very small amount of time and a few souls are exchanged."
She explained.
"So you are saying... I wassupposed tocome here...
I wassupposed toget the System I got...
And—"
"Yes."
The Seer nodded, knowing exactly what Nux wanted to ask.
"While it may not all be the complete truth, most of what your Father explained to you was his arrangement."
"So he... really is my Father..."
Nux’s eyes shined and again, the Seer nodded.
"Not a good one.
He didn’t have your best interest in his heart, you were correct not to trust him from the beginning."
"So you knew his plan..."
Nux noted and the Seer didn’t hide it either, in fact, she revealed more facts.
"I did not just know his plans.
I know he succeeded.
Or at least...
He should have succeeded."
"What...?"
Nux’s expression changed and the Seer nodded.
"Zylarith Chaosveil was supposed to win the battle between the Infinities and rule the Universe."
"Wait..."
Nux paused for a moment.
"You... know what was... supposed to happen...?"
"Weren’t you listening? That Universe was the same as any Universe, I knew its past, present and future, just like I did with other Universes.
Everything only changed when... you entered Lilith’s Illusion and formed what you called the Black Hole."
"The beginning of my Universe..."
Nux muttered and the Seer nodded.
"So wait, Zylarith was supposed to win...?"
Nux asked curiously.
"That is correct."
The Seer nodded, then, since she already knew what Nux was going to ask next, she answered—
"Your first meeting was mostly the same, he came to you and told you to use your wives as tools to get stronger, you rejected him.
That day, he went away.
But he had another plan."
"Sharnoth Nocthys..."
Nux narrowed his eyes.
And again, the Seer nodded.
"Yes.
He prepared Sharnoth Nocthys. She was supposed to meet you, guide you in the Universe, then, according to Zylarith’s instructions, fall in love with you.
Through the System, you were supposed to take the Body of Chaos from her. Then, you were supposed to master the Body of Chaos and—"
The Seer didn’t need to complete those words.
"The moment I mastered the Body of Chaos, he would have taken control over my body."
"Yes.
From that point, he would have taken over your body that had turned into a perfect vessel for him because of the System, used it to grow his army further.
Then, once his consciousness took over your mind and you lost yourself.

He would have revealed Azriel’s existence, had him killed and Yrniel destroyed. Then he would have found the Fifth Supreme World after three more reincarnation cycles, taken over it, used it to become an Infinity.
And attacked the Four Infinities, who were severely weakened after their battle with Azriel."
Nux blinked, none of this surprised him since he could see it happening, but it was still interesting to hear how things weresupposedto play out.
"So Lord Azriel would have lost, huh..."
He muttered, a little taken aback.
"Well, it wasn’t exactly a fair battle."
The Seer shrugged.
"He was restricted to Yrniel, Zylarith revealed that. So the moment the Infinities destroyed Yrniel, Azriel lost quite a bit of his strength, ultimately losing the final battle.
Though even when he was weakened, there would have been some instances where he would have won if things went his way, you can say he was just... unlucky in some regard."
The Seer explained, then she looked at Nux and—
"Though there are some Universes where Lord Azriel has won and has gone on to become the Universe’s God."
She added since she felt like he would like to know.
"Is that so..."
"Indeed.
Although by that logic, there are Universes where Seraphielle won, Ul’Thakar, Equarios, Orravyn, many of their versions have won in their respective Universes as well.
Some Universes remain without a victor till the very end.
Some Universes, actually, many of them have entirely different Gods.
The Multiverse is vast.
It is quite amusing to see how a presumably simple change can create an entirely different Universe, with an entirely different Timeline."
Nux nodded at that information, he definitely appreciated it. Thinking about how itcould have gonewas definitely interesting.
But—
As Nux looked at the woman standing before him, he couldn’t help but wonder.
This was the woman who... understood the Multiverse probably more than any being in the entirety of existence.
She was someone who knew the past, present and the future of every single Universe.
Just...
What sort of existence did one have to be to know what... she knew...?

The more he looked at her, the stronger his interest became, not romantically, maybe because he was still being affected by his rage, but the current Nux had no romantic feelings or desire for this woman, he was just... curious.
"What are you?"
He asked a direct question.
A question that the Seer obviously expected but for some reason, it still startled her nonetheless.
Her startled expression, however, did not stop Nux. He just narrowed his eyes as he looked at her and—
"You said that no being with a Physical Body, a Soul, or any connection to any Universe, can exist in the Multiverse then...
Who are you?
How did you come here?
How did you even know this place existed?"
He asked a series of questions.
But then—
As his mind moved, as he began thinking of the possible answers, all his questions changed and he asked one, simple question.
"Who killed you?"

Some Universes, actually, many of them have entirely different Gods.
The Multiverse is vast.
It is quite amusing to see how a presumably simple change can create an entirely different Universe, with an entirely different Timeline."
Nux nodded at that information, he definitely appreciated it.
Thinking about how itcould have gonewas definitely interesting.
But—
As Nux looked at the woman standing before him, he couldn’t help but wonder.
This was the woman who... understood the Multiverse probably more than any being in the entirety of existence.
She was someone who knew the past, present and the future of every single Universe.
Just...
What sort of existence did one have to be to know what... she knew...?

The more he looked at her, the stronger his interest became, not romantically, maybe because he was still being affected by his rage, but the current Nux had no romantic feelings or desire for this woman, he was just... curious.
"What are you?"
He asked a direct question.
A question that the Seer obviously expected but for some reason, it still startled her nonetheless.
Her startled expression, however, did not stop Nux.
He just narrowed his eyes as he looked at her and—
"You said that no being with a Physical Body, a Soul, or any connection to any Universe, can exist in the Multiverse then...
Who are you?
How did you come here?
How did you even know this place existed?"
He asked a series of questions.
But then—
As his mind moved, as he began thinking of the possible answers, all his questions changed and he asked one, simple question.
"Who killed you?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2373: Avernyth Eternity.
paragraphs: "Who killed you?"
Nux asked directly.
No Physical Body.
No Soul.
No connection to any Universe.
These were the conditions to enter the Multiverse.
Let’s not even mention the fact that knowing these conditions itself was next to impossible—
There weren’t many beings in a Universe who could kill one being while fulfilling all these conditions.
There were three kinds of Death.
A normal death, where one’s physical body perishes.
This is where the Soul survives, returns to the Universe and is reincarnated into a new life.
Second is Erasure.
This one’s more uncommon. While many beings in the Universe understand the concept of Soul and know of its existence, a very few could... erase it.
This is where neither a physical body remains, nor a Soul.
And last but not the least—
It’s what happened to Nux.
Where not only was his Physical Body ruined and his Soul erased—
His very existence was removed.
His connection with the Universe, his Bonds, his Links, the people’s memories of him—
Everything was erased.
Almost no being in the Universe had the capability to pull off something this grand, if Nux had to guess only...
The Infinities could do it.
And if the Seer was here, it meant she was killed like this, meaning that the being who killed her... was an Infinity.
Then...
The question arises—
Who was she?
For an Infinity to kill her in a way he did—
What did she do to offend him?
What was her past?
What kind of existence was she in the past?
All these questions overwhelmed Nux’s mind. Of course, he also considered the possibility of the Seer being from an entirely different Universe.
In fact, that sounded more plausible.
Maybe she was one of the Infinities from some other Universe and died fighting other Infinities of her Universe.
But...
For some reason—
As Nux looked at her and he remembered all of his interactions with her...
He felt like... that wasn’t the case...
That the story was somewhat different than what seemed to be the most plausible possibility.
And he was correct.
"Your Father killed me."
The Seer revealed the truth and even though something in his heart already told him the answer to his question, he still asked.
"Was it... Zylarith that I know...?"
"That is correct."
The Seer nodded and the instant Nux confirmed what he was thinking was true—
An answer came to his mind and his eyes widened in surprise.
"You are...
Avernyth Eternity."
"You arrived there quicker than I expected.
That must mean you have already consumed Zylarith’s memories."
The Seer chuckled.
And the moment she confirmed Nux’s words, his eyes widened even further.
"You really are her..."
He spoke like a radio that was stuck at one point and couldn’t move further and he couldn’t be blamed either.
Avernyth Eternity.
The woman who sacrificed her life to save the Universe from Zylarith.
The previous Infinity of Eternity, the Mother of Orravyn Eternity and... the shadow Orravyn had been chasing all his life but could never reach.
That was Avernyth Eternity.
The woman even Zylarith Chaosveil respected and, at some level, feared.
A woman who was said to have advanced the Universe at a rate so quick that their Universe developed a few trillion years faster than it should have.
A woman whose death was mourned by most of the Universe, even today, because while Orravyn had taken her place—
Not a single one of Orravyn’s inventions or discoveries, could even come close to things his mother discovered on a regular basis.
"Wait... but that doesn’t make any sense..."
Suddenly, Nux frowned in confusion.
He had Zylarith’s memories and according to them—
"The Seer existed even when Avernyth did. There were times when Zylarith had seen the two of them together.
Then if you are the Seer then how are you also..."
Nux didn’t complete his sentence. He didn’t have to either, because the Seer understood what he was trying to say and she just laughed.
"Well, I am notjustAvernyth."
She answered with a shrug.
"You are Avernythandthe Seer...?"
Nux asked and the Seer’s smile widened.
"I am Avernyth and Vashti.
Actually, in some way, I am more Vashti, than I am Avernyth."
"What...? Vashti...?"
Nux blinked.
And in an instant—
An image appeared in his head.
The woman he had met back in the Temple of Time. The woman the Infinities had cruelly used against him, the woman those bastards tormented.
"You are... Vashti...?"
Nux couldn’t help but frown.
"Yes, as Vashti, I cleared all the Trials in the Temple of Time, learned about the Multiverse and the conditions to come here, then I manipulated Zylarith into killing me, Avernyth, to get here—
Ultimately becoming what I am today—
The Seer."
The Seer explained in a calm, light tone, almost as if she was telling a bedtime story even children would understand without much effort.
And...
The more she spoke—
The less Nux understood.
"But Vashti never completed all of the Temple of Time’s Trials, she was caught by the Infinities before that—"
"That wasn’t supposed to happen."
The Seer shook her head.

"It only happened because your existence corrupted the Timeline. The Infinities weren’t supposed to learn about Vashti and Vashti was supposed to clear the Temple of Time, ultimately Transcending her understanding of Time, learning about the Multiverse and ultimately coming here as Avernyth.
Or in other words...
Me."
"No no no no."
Nux shook his head again and again—
"This isn’t about what wassupposedto happen. It is about whathashappened. Vashti was caught and even if you made the deal with the Infinities to release her in exchange for giving me to them.
It isn’t clear whether they would honor their end of the bargain, not when you went against your promise first.
Not to mention I have seen Vashti’s memories through Zylarith’s memories, she has no record of being a Seer.
Just what are you talking about?"
Nux’s frown deepened.
From Zylarith’s memories, he knew what the Infinities had done with Vashti, he also knew that before the Seer came to him, she went to Zylarith and the other Infinities and offered a deal.
Him in exchange for Vashti’s body, a deal the Infinities accepted in an instant and agreed to release Vashti and return her to her natural state as long as the Seer held her end of the bargain.
But the thing was—

According to Zylarith’s memories, while he didn’t particularly care about Vashti since most of his focus was on him, he didn’t think the rest of the Infinities were going to hold their end of the bargain.
Especially not now, when they didn’t actually get his body and were forced to kill him instead.
Not to mention, even if they did hold up their bargain just so they did not offend the Seer—
Every single one of them had noticed a link between Vashti and the Seer, they would definitely keep a constant eye on the Girl just so they could know more about the Seer.
There was absolutely no way Vashti would be able to return to the Temple of Time, let alone clear the rest of the Trials.
Then—
How does the Seer even exist at this point...?

chapters.title: Chapter 2374: You should not exist.
paragraphs: How does the Seer even exist at this point...?
Also, even if he were to believe her story—
"Your explanation itself doesn’t make sense either.
You say you learned about the Multiverse after you cleared all of the Trials in the Temple of Time, then you manipulated Zylarith into killing Avernyth.
But...
Vashti wasn’t even born when Avernyth arrived and if you went to the past as Vashti, then that should have created another branch and ultimately a different Universe."

Nux spoke out his thoughts, the flaws in the Seer’s explanation couldn’t be more obvious, if he had heard this story from anyone else, at any point in time, he would have called it bullshit and would have given a one-star review for lack of smart writing in the fantasy story.
But...
For some odd reason—

Even when his mind could see the obvious flaws in the story, as he saw the woman standing in front of him with a calm look on her face, he couldn’t help but have this nagging feeling that... whatever she was saying was the truth.
And it was.
"You are trying to simplify things that cannot be simplified."
The Seer answered with a light smile on her face. Then, she looked at the vast space they were in and—
"You are in a Multiverse."
She informed.
"A space where no living entity should be in the first place, and yet...
Here you are.
You say my explanation doesn’t make sense, that it sounds impossible but..."
The Seer turned back to him and—
"The very fact that you are here talking to me is an impossibility."
"Do not try to change the subject."
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"I am not trying to change the subject, I am trying to say that things are far more complicated than the picture you have in your mind."
"Explain the complications to me then."
Nux didn’t back down.
He was serious when he said he would only accept whatever the Seer had to offer once she told him the truth. He would no longer trust her on empty words.
The Seer looked at him and... at some level, she knew this was exactly how he would react.
So she just sighed—
"You are in a Multiverse."
She repeated her sentence.
"What you see in front of you are countless Universes that exist simultaneously."
Nux didn’t interrupt, he let her continue and the Seer did—
"And while the depiction of Universes you see here may confuse you, do not be fooled.
The Concept of Time does not exist in the Multiverse.
It only exists individually, in individual Universes, or in other words, the Concept of Time only exists for beings that are part of the Universe.
But for the Multiverse—
Past, Present and Future do not come one after the other.
For the Multiverse, everything, about every particular Universe, be it its Beginning, its End, the Time when the Universe is conquered by a God—
It is all happening simultaneously."
The Seer explained and...
"...what?"
Nux had absolutely no clue what she just said.
The Seer then looked at him and—
"The Multiverse doesn’t carewhenan entity named Vashti cleared the Temple of Time, from its perspective, it will happen, it is happening, and it has happened—
All at the same time."
She explained and finally, Nux’s expression began to change.
"So according to the Multiverse, the time when Vashti has cleared the Temple of Time and the time when Zylarith erases Avernyth is... no different.
So even if you went to the past, manipulated Zylarith to kill Avernyth, the Multiverse will not notice that you fooled it."
He spoke and the Seer chuckled—
"While I am glad you have such a high opinion of me, I do not possess the ability totrickit.
I did not fool the Multiverse, Nux.
It is exactly how it is supposed to work."
"So... the moment Zylarith killed you as Avernyth...
You arrived here on your own?"
"That would be a more accurate way to put it, yes."
The Seer nodded.
"It must have confused you."
Nux commented. He couldn’t imagine dying and then appearing in a place like this with absolutely no one telling him what this was and where he was.
Even when he came here, if it wasn’t for her telling him what she did, he would still be looking around with a foolish look on his face, while trying to understand where he was.
But then—
"No, I knew."
"...what?"
Now Nux frowned again.
"I tricked Zylarith into killing me, remember? It amuses me how they still think Isacrificedmyself for the greater good."
She laughed but Nux wasn’t the least bit amused. He was now even more confused.
"How did you, as Avernyth, know you were supposed to trick Zylarith when Vashti didn’t even exist at that..."
Before Nux completed his words, he turned silent on his own. He was still confused, he felt like he knew the answer, but at the same time, he didn’t.
The Seer looked at him and chuckled—

"You are still looking at things through the Concept of Time. The momentIbecame the Seer, both my incarnations, Vashti and Avernyth, were no longer part of the Universe, the Concept of Time did not exist for them any longer.
Avernyth knew about Vashti, Vashti knew about Avernyth, and both of them did what was supposed to be done to create...
Me."
She explained in the simplest way possible.
"But I read Vashti’s memories..."
Nux repeated the same point.
He had seen Vashti’s memories through Zylarith’s mind and he did not see any memories related to Avernyth or the Seer.
"What you saw was the distorted version of Vashti in a timeline that you corrupted."
The Seer answered and Nux—
"This is exactly what I have been trying to say ALL THIS WHILE!"
He raised his voice.

"Icorruptedthe Timeline, I changed the Universe’s present and altered its future, because of me, Vashti is captured, because of me, Vashti would never be able to clear the Temple of Time, because of me, she would never learn about the existence of the Multiverse, ultimately, Avernyth would never learn about the existence of the Multiverse—
So what I am trying to say is—
Youshould not exist."

chapters.title: Chapter 2375: So you are alive because... the Multiverse hates me?
paragraphs: "So what I am trying to say is—
Youshould not exist."
Nux spoke with an absolutely serious look on his face and the Seer just laughed—
"You should be the last person saying that, Nux."
Nux didn’t know how he was supposed to counter it.
He... was a living Universe.
While that in itself was an Anomaly, that in itself made him different from other living beings, but even when compared to other Universes...
He was the only Universe that had an entirely different Concept of Time.
Even amongst the countless Universes, he... was an Anomaly.
A Multiversal Anomaly.
An existence even the Multiverse had decided to just... ignore.
He should be the last person to say the words he just said.
The Seer smiled when she saw his reaction, as if she knew exactly what he was thinking, but then, she explained—
"I onlyshould not existbecause you exist.
But in the eyes of the Multiverse, you do not exist.
Ending my existence would be accepting your existence, and the Multiverse would not do that."
"So you are alive because... the Multiverse hates me?"
Nux tilted his head and the Seer—
"In a certain sense, yes."
She laughed.
Nux didn’t know what he was supposed to say or feel.
He thought about it for a moment and then—
"But what about the changes my existence caused? Thereasonfor your existence no longer exists, shouldn’t you... do something about it?
Is that why you asked for Vashti’s body from the Infinities in return for giving me to them?"
He asked with a curious look on his face and the Seer, she just shrugged.
"That’s the Multiverse’s problem to deal with.
As for asking for Vashti’s body, I only did that so those five do not doubt me. They would never trust me if I helped them without asking anything in return."
Nux looked at her with a deadpan look on his face.
"So from the start... all you really cared about was getting me surrounded by the Infinities so they could kill me the way you wanted them to and send me here huh..."
He muttered with an understanding look on his face but just then—
"Well..."
The Seer looked away, almost as if she was trying to avoid that topic. Nux noticed that and that made him narrow his eyes.
He moved and appeared where the Seer was looking, the woman looked away again and—
"You know you are being obvious, right? Almost purposefully so."
"I... do not wish to hide anything but I do not know how to say it either..."
The Seer answered with a hesitant look on her face.
"Say it."
But Nux was different.

chapters.title: Chapter 2376: I made a move.
paragraphs: "That is correct.
I gave you Bloodedge because it has the ability to connect two Universes as long as there is a medium.
I was hoping for the Bloodedge to sense me from wherever you were and connect you to the Multiverse."
The Seer revealed and Nux narrowed his eyes.
"Ability to connect two Universes as long as... there is a medium?"

Nux frowned, then he recalled how the Bloodedge connected Zylarith’s Chaos to the Main Universe’s Chaos to create an opening the Infinities used to force their way inside his dimension and his frown deepened.
"What was the medium?"
He asked directly.
As far as he knew, there was no Energy or Power in that Dark place, neither could he sense anything here in the Multiverse.
Then...
What medium did the sword use?
"It’s me."
The Seer answered with a light smile and Nux’s frown deepened.
"You...? How did you become... a medium...?"
"You have Zylarith’s memories, do you not?
Then you must know how Relics are made?"

Nux nodded with a disgusted look on his face. He wasn’t a Saint, in fact, he could even be called a mass murderer, but the moment he learned about the technique to create Relics, he felt sick to his core.
To use a living being’s Soul to do—
Before Nux could complete his thought, his thought process froze as he noticed something else.
The Bloodedge...
It was a Relic as well...
And...
It was no ordinary Relic.
It was a Relic that was strong enough to kill even the Infinities.
While the strength of a Relic depends on quite a few factors, one of the most important factors is the strength of the Soul it is being made out of...
For a Relic to be strong enough to kill Infinities... the Soul required to make it would be...
"Avernyth Eternity..."
Nux let out a name and...
"That is correct."
The Seer nodded.
"You used your own Soul to create the Bloodedge, that was the medium it used to sense... you."
Again, the Seer nodded and the more Nux thought about it, the more horrifying it all began.

To think he had been carrying the Soul of an Infinity as a weapon all this time. No wonder the Bloodedge was so ridiculously strong and used that much energy. He literally owned the Soul of an Infinity!
Soon however, Nux frowned again.
"No, if... Avernyth’s Soul is with me...
Then how did... Vashti come into existence?
Did you... divide Avernyth’s Soul into two?"
"In some way, yes."
The Seer nodded.
But Nux shook his head.
That answer did not satisfy him.
"No, I need a proper answer."
He demanded.
Because too many things didn’t line up here.
Even if he believed her story.
The Seer came into existence because Vashti learned about the Multiverse and Avernyth was killed the way one had to be killed to enter the Multiverse.
But going with that logic—
Avernyth’s Soul shouldn’t even exist in the first place.
Then how was it inside Bloodedge all this while?
Also, if he was not who he was in the original timeline, then why would Avernyth create a Sword using her own Soul? That too, a Sword that was clearly made just for the current version of him.
The Seer looked at him and then—
"I made a move."
She told the truth.
"You made... a move...?"
Nux tilted his head in confusion.
"For quindecillions of years, I have only been observing the Multiverse from the sidelines, like an observer who was watching a movie play out.
I knew the past, I knew the present and I knew the future of countless Universes.
At first, I enjoyed it.
Both as Vashti and Avernyth, I craved knowledge more than power, to me, knowledgewaspower.
To know everything there was to know about the Universe.
That was when I learned about the Multiverse, a world even bigger than a Universe, a... forest of Universes.
That lit a light in me, I wanted to see, I wanted to understand the Multiverse, I wanted to find out the truth of existence, the start of it all and I wanted to see the end.
Every secret that the Multiverse held, I wanted to know it.
That fire inside me that constantly craved knowledge, that was what kept me going.
The more I learned, the more I wanted to learn but eventually—
After every single sacrifice I made, after I learned every single thing about every single Universe, after I had answers to every single question that once bothered me—
I realized something.
I was no longer a living entity.
In pursuit of knowledge, I gave up my body, my soul, my connection and my right to live in every single Universe.
The knowledge that I so deeply craved ended up becoming a curse that pulled me away from Life itself.
I only became an observer.
An observer who knew everything that was supposed to happen in every single Universe, but could never physically interact with any of the said Universes."
The Seer explained, looking at the Multiverse with a distant look on her face. Then, she slowly turned towards Nux and—
"That was when you appeared."
"Of course, your appearance in itself never surprised me, you weresupposed toappear. My projection in your Universe simply noted your existence and didn’t think much of it anymore.
But that was when it happened—
Something that should not have happened.
You...
You didn’t move how you were supposed to move and that surprised me. I looked into you more clearly and then I saw it."
The Seer’s tone changed, her monotony changing to excitement, as if recalling that moment still excited her.
She then pointed at Nux’s Universe and—
"That was the first time your Universe appeared.
A Universe that is different than any other Universe, a Universe with no clear future, a Universe that I couldn’t even visit, let alone study and understand.
And then..."
The Seer then turned to the Universe Nux and her initially belonged to, the so-called ’Main Universe’ and—
"Then the Timeline that has always been constant, the Timeline that has always been unchanging...
Changed.
And the Future—
It no longer existed because you corrupted it."

chapters.title: Chapter 2377: Fling... it...?
paragraphs: "Then the Timeline that has always been constant, the Timeline that has always been unchanging...
Changed.
And the Future—
It no longer existed because you corrupted it."
The Seer spoke, not hiding her excitement one bit. Nux looked at her, overwhelmed by the strong emotions she was showing, this was the first time he had seen her express this much emotion.
"Was that... a good thing?"
He asked, a little taken aback and the Seer grinned, not the polite playful smile she always had, she actually grinned.
"I did not know."
She answered.
"What I did know, however, was that this was my chance.
Your existence alone has made a mess out of the Timeline and there was nothing the Multiverse could do about it.
This was my only chance.
To release myself from the trap that I had fallen into.
To leave this place for good.
To...
To live.
So I made a decision.
I used you as a veil to... make a few moves myself."
"What moves?"
Nux asked.
"I appeared in front of Avernyth."
"Oh?"
Nux tilted his head.
"If I had done that before, it would have simply created another branch in the Multiverse, giving birth to another Universe that would have been of no help to me whatsoever.
But this time—
Because your existence had corrupted the Universe, it did not branch. So I took an even bolder step, I overwhelmed Avernyth’s memories with mine and took over her body."
"You... took over Avernyth’s body...?"
Nux blinked.
How does... one take over her own... body?
He wondered in his head.
"That action wouldn’t have just made another branch, I am a being who is now part of the Multiverse, I was not supposed to return to existence.
Normally, that action should have erased that branch and ended my existence with it since the Multiverse would have corrected what was wrong.
But because of the disruption you caused, the Multiverse didn’t sense it.
So I took over Avernyth’s body and I used her Soul to create the Bloodedge for you."
"Why her soul...?"
Nux couldn’t help but ask.
"Because it was strong and it was connected to me."
The Seer answered.
"Strong because the weapon you wanted to create must be strong and...
Connected to you because you later wanted to use this to pull me to the Multiverse."
"That is correct."
The Seer nodded again.
"Then shouldn’t removing Avernyth’s Soul from the equation end your existence as well because Zylarith wouldn’t have been able to kill you...
No, you already exist.
So that would be another problem the Multiverse needs to deal with."
Nux answered his own question.
"You are getting the hang of it, aren’t you?"
She chuckled.
"But then why are Zylarith’s memories a mess, because according to him, he killed Avernyth."
"Oh he did."
The Seer nodded.

"I didn’t simplyremoveAvernyth from the equation, I only knew the Fixed Future, that was my only advantage. Your existence erased that fixed future, so any action from here on out could change everything that I know of.
So I needed to make sure everything went as closely as it did in the Original Timeline, till you appeared and made a mess of it.
So yes, Zylarith did kill me as Avernyth but my Soul simply went to Bloodedge that I had linked myself to before he could erase it.
And of course, he never knew."
The Seer shrugged, as if fooling that time’s strongest being in the Universe wasn’t a big deal at all.
"So that’s how it all happened..."
Nux nodded.
Then, he looked at the Seer and—
"This is also the reason why when they erased my connections, my connection with the Bloodedge did not disappear because technically...
Bloodedge shouldn’t even exist in the Timeline, so the Multiverse does not consider its existence."
He spoke out loud and once again—
"You are right again."
She seemed glad that Nux was absorbing everything so quickly. It had been a long time since she had such a genuine, true conversation with anyone.
"What made you so sure that Bloodedge’s connection would take me to the Multiverse?"
Nux asked curiously.
"I wasn’t sure."
The Seer answered honestly.
"You weren’t, huh..."
Nux didn’t even seem surprised at this point, after all, the Seer had already said this before.

"I knew what happens to the beings who are erased like you were, I knew your remaining conscious thoughts would drift into an empty dark space, where eventually, people lose their sense of self and disappear permanently.
And I hoped that the Bloodedge would be able to use the Energy it had been absorbing from you all this while and form an opening that brings you to me."
She explained.
And it was exactly what happened, so in some distorted way, her plan did succeed.
But Nux...
He just looked at the woman in front of him and—
"And...
How exactly did you think, *I*, who was merely a consciousness without any form of body, was supposed to use that opening you so generously provided?"
Nux asked with eyes that wanted to kill the woman in front of him and once again, the Seer looked away.
"Answer my question, woman."
Nux spoke in a stricter tone.
The Seer looked even further away, Nux followed her gaze, still waiting for an answer and the Seer, she—
I thought you would just... fling it..."
"Fling... it...?"
Nux repeated those words with an absurd look on his face.
One had to know—
This was the most knowledgeable woman in all of the Multiverse, a woman who was supposed to know EVERYTHING.
A woman who had consumed so much knowledge, that she now knows the beginning, the present, and the future of every single Universe in the Multiverse.
And the answer a woman like her came up with was...
Fling it...?
Nux couldn’t believe it.
It all just felt so ridiculous that he wanted to pull this woman’s hair off, he, however, tried to hold himself back and with a pretentiously calm look on his face—
"And what if I... wasn’t able to...fling it...?"
He asked.
"Then we both die."
The Seer answered.
And Nux—
Now he really did want to pull this woman’s hair off.

"What made you so sure that Bloodedge’s connection would take me to the Multiverse?"
Nux asked curiously.
"I wasn’t sure."
The Seer answered honestly.
"You weren’t, huh..."
Nux didn’t even seem surprised at this point, after all, the Seer had already said this before.

"I knew what happens to the beings who are erased like you were, I knew your remaining conscious thoughts would drift into an empty dark space, where eventually, people lose their sense of self and disappear permanently.
And I hoped that the Bloodedge would be able to use the Energy it had been absorbing from you all this while and form an opening that brings you to me."
She explained.
And it was exactly what happened, so in some distorted way, her plan did succeed.
But Nux...
He just looked at the woman in front of him and—
"And...
How exactly did you think, *I*, who was merely a consciousness without any form of body, was supposed to use that opening you so generously provided?"
Nux asked with eyes that wanted to kill the woman in front of him and once again, the Seer looked away.
"Answer my question, woman."
Nux spoke in a stricter tone.
The Seer looked even further away, Nux followed her gaze, still waiting for an answer and the Seer, she—
I thought you would just... fling it..."
"Fling... it...?"
Nux repeated those words with an absurd look on his face.
One had to know—
This was the most knowledgeable woman in all of the Multiverse, a woman who was supposed to know EVERYTHING.
A woman who had consumed so much knowledge, that she now knows the beginning, the present, and the future of every single Universe in the Multiverse.
And the answer a woman like her came up with was...
Fling it...?
Nux couldn’t believe it.
It all just felt so ridiculous that he wanted to pull this woman’s hair off, he, however, tried to hold himself back and with a pretentiously calm look on his face—
"And what if I... wasn’t able to...fling it...?"
He asked.
"Then we both die."
The Seer answered.
And Nux—
Now he really did want to pull this woman’s hair off.
