paragraphs: "And what if I... wasn’t able to...fling it...?"
Nux asked as he tried to control his anger.
"Then we both die."
The Seer answered.
And Nux—
Now he really was about to lose his mind, especially when he heard those last words.
"Webothdie...?
Woman, at worst, you would only return to being the observer you have always been.Iam the one who would have lost my life, my wives, my children and my Universe.
OnlyI stood to lose from it."
"No, that is untrue."
The Seer shook her head.
"I used you as a veil, so the moment you are gone, my veil is gone, the Multiverse sees what I did and I cease to exist, permanently."
"That doesn’t make sense."
Nux frowned.
"Couldn’t it simply create another branch? Another separate Universe where you visited Avernyth and took over her body?"
He wondered, after all, this didn’t exactly seem like a big thing considering there were already... Nux couldn’t even count how many Universes there were...
Tredecillion, Quattuordecillion, Quindecillion or maybe more—
Too many.
But the Seer shook her head.
"Our Universe can no longer be branched.
This is also the reason another Universe where you did whatever you did, did not appear while the Timeline of that Universe was preserved."
"Why is that?"
Nux asked with a frown.
"Because of Avernyth."
Nux’s frown deepened, he thought about it for a moment, then, his mind came up with his own reasoning—
"Is it because Avernyth was erased...?"
The Seer’s smile widened, as if she was impressed.
"Exactly."
She nodded.
"Avernyth was erased from all timelines, no version of her exists in any of the Universes throughout the Multiverse, except for in one Universe."
"Our Universe."
Nux muttered and once again, the Seer nodded.
"Why wasn’t she erased from our Universe as well?"
He asked with a frown on his face.
Wasn’t that what being ’Erased’ means?
"She is essentially erased.
The name Avernyth Eternity isn’t known even when she was once the Infinity of Eternity."
Nux nodded at that.
He always found it odd, he had memories of countless worlds, many of those worlds existed in Avernyth’s Era, but never once did he hear her name. People usually called her the Infinity of Eternity.
Even now, the people who knew of her existence called her the Previous Eternity, or the Current Infinity of Eternity, Orravyn’s Mother.
And it wasn’t even aboutknowing or not knowingthe name, the people didn’t even bother to find out.
Nux had never heard a question like—
Who was the Previous Eternity?
What was her name?
What was her power?
Even he was no different.
He showed no interest in her either, almost as if... she didn’t even exist in the first place.
It was only after he read Zylarith’s memory that he was finally able to put a name, face and the rest of the details on the blurred figure in his mind.
"The only reason our Universe still has the memory of Avernyth Eternity is because the beings who remember her, the Infinities, are too strong to be affected by the erasure.
Unlike other beings in the Universe, their minds are simply too powerful to just... forget."
The Seer explained.
But that made Nux think of another question—
"Then what about Avernyth in other Universes? Wouldn’t the Infinities of those Universes know her as well? How did they forget about her?"
"They didn’t forget about her."
The Seer corrected.
"Avernyth never existed there in the first place.
That is what it means to be erased."
"No no."
Nux shook his head.
"I am asking about the time when an Avernythdidexist in those Univer—"
Nux asked, he however, stopped in the middle of his own question as he realized it—
"Time does not exist in the Multiverse."
The Seer smiled again.
"Correct.
The moment Avernyth was erased, her existence was removed from every single Universe."
The Seer then looked at Nux and—
"Just like yours, your wives, and every single entity you have devoured till now has."
"...what?"
Nux’s expression changed.
"What? You didn’t know?"
The Seer raised her eyebrow.
"I knew I do not exist in any of the Universes, but my wives..."
"No, you won’t find ’other versions’ of your wives in other Universes. They and every being you have devoured, do not exist in the eyes of the Multiverse."
"Is that so..."
Nux nodded to himself.
He was honestly... glad about this.
This way—
His wives would be completely his.
He wouldn’t have to go through quindecillions of Universes to take his wives away from them.
Mind you, hewas very muchplanning to do it if it came to it.
The Seer looked at him, then she just chuckled, not saying anything.
Then suddenly—
"So if I was gone, your ’veil’ would be gone too and the Multiverse will be after you since creating a Branch isn’t possible."
Nux summarized.
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"Why doesn’t the Multiverse get rid of me as well? You may have used me as a veil, but I am the cause of this problem. Why does it not target me?"
He asked.
"It is because it cannot."
And the Seer answered.
"It... cannot...?"
Nux raised his eyebrow.
The Seer then pointed at the vast Multiverse in front of her and—
"You see it? Every single Universe is interconnected, this network of connection is what’s called theMultiverse.
You, however, aren’t part of the Multiverse."
She explained, pointing at Nux’s Universe that had no connection to the Multiverse or any Universe whatsoever.
"You exist on your own."
"And the Multiverse cannot get rid of what does not belong to it."
Nux completed that sentence and once again, the Seer nodded.
"This is why you are so important to me.
This is the reason only you can give me what I want."
"What is it that you want?"
Nux asked.
But the Seer, she shook her head again and—
"First, you accept my Gift."
Nux thought about it for a moment, he thought about everything he was told, everything he had learned in this little time, then, he looked at the Seer and—
"Can... I return to my wives if I accept your gift?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2379: The Law of Origin.
paragraphs: "Can... I return to my wives if I accept your gift?"
Nux asked as he looked at her with a determined look on his face. As if the moment the Seer said yes, whatever it was, he was going to accept it.
But...
"I do not know."
The Seer answered honestly.
"You said I could."
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"In theory, yes.
But...

We are already standing in the territory of the unknown, what I even call atheory, isn’t a theory by definition, it is merely a prediction I made after observing the Multiverse all this while and can undeniably be affected by my wish for it to be true."
"So you arranged all this, turning your own Soul into a relic, having yourself be killed, planning my death, then risking my life hoping it would work out, all of it—
On a whim?"
The Seer didn’t say anything.
While Nux’s words were an extremely diluted version of everything she had planned, thought and done so far—
At their very core—
What she did was nothing more than a desperate move to get out of this hell and... live.
So yes, she did it allon a whimand if she had a choice—
She would do it all over again.
Nux looked at her for a good while, none of them knew how much time had passed, or if time had passed at all.
But in the end—
"Alright."
Nux bit it.
"What’s your gift?"
He asked.
What choice did he even have?
He was stuck in a place he knew next to nothing about, with no way of returning, his physical body, his Soul and his connection to his own Universe erased—
He couldn’t sense his wives, he couldn’t sense his children, he couldn’t sense... anything.
All he could see was this ridiculously vast Multiverse that held basically no meaning to him since his wives weren’t next to him.
So yes.
He was desperate.
And in his desperation, he had no choice but to seek the Seer’s help, again, after being betrayed by her once.
"If you betray me again..."
He muttered.
The Seer looked at him, he looked at her face and then, he just sighed—
"I don’t even know what I would do or who I’d be angrier at, you or myself."
"It would be you."
The Seer answered with certainty.
"I did not want you to answer that."
Nux felt his mouth twitching as the Seer nodded, she looked a little sheepish as she did that. It was cute.
Nux, however, shook his head.
"Now tell me what your gift is."
He demanded and once again, the Seer pointed at the Multiverse in front of him.
"I wish to gift you my ability."
She explained.
"The ability... you have...?"
"You see this vast Multiverse?"
"Yes, it is pretty hard to miss."
"There are nine vigintillion, seven hundred eighty-four novemdecillion, six hundred thirteen octodecillion Universes in here."
She took a small pause, as if she wanted Nux to digest what she just said, and then, she dropped an even bigger bomb.
"I can visit any one of these Universes, at any point in time, be it its beginning, its end, or a particular event that I desire."
"But you do not have a physical body, so you cannot properly interact with any of these Universes."

Nux pointed out, he had learned enough from their conversation. The Seer expected that, actually, the more Nux understood from their conversation and started inferring things on his own, the more confident she became that this might work out the way she expected it to.
"That is correct."
She nodded.
"I cannot interact with those Universes because of the Multiverse’s restriction but..."
She looked at him, Nux narrowed his eyes when he saw her expression, then, he tilted his head—
"Are you saying that I... can...?"
"The Multiverse has no Authority over you because you do not belong to it, so if you learn how to enter and leave any Universe you please and are able to interact with it, then—"
"Then I can return to my own Universe and my wives."
Nux interrupted as the light in his eyes shined at the possibility.
"Exactly."
The Seer nodded and the more Nux thought about it, the more believable it all looked.
"Alright then, let’s do it.
Tell me how I am supposed to do what you do."
He asked.
After all, while the Seer said she could enter any Universe at any point in time, he didn’t have that ability, neither had he seen the Seer do it in front of him.
All he could see right now was the Multiverse, he didn’t even know if the branches the Seer had pointed out were the actual Universes, let alone being able to enter them.
From here, he couldn’t interact with any of them.
"Well, I can’t exactly justtellyou how I do it."
The Seer slowed him down.
"You need to learn it."
"How am I supposed to learn if you do not teach me?"
Nux frowned. Then, he thought of another thing and—
"Let me read your memories, I will learn what I need to on my own."
The Seer however, just laughed at those words.
"Don’t bother.
You will be overwhelmed.
I have quindecillions of years’ worth of memories in my head and this is just what I recall—
If you read my memories from the beginning, you will simply lose yourself and lose your own consciousness."
Nux didn’t say anything.
If anyone else had said these words to him, he would have laughed it off. Nux had literal Worlds’ worth of memories in his head, even the memories of an Infinity couldn’t overwhelm him.
But—
While he did have Worlds’ worth of memories in him, at best, it was only a few hundred quintillion.
It was... nowhere near the number the Seer just mentioned.
If there was any being who could overwhelm his mind with her memories, it was her.
The only being whose brain held more information than his...
Nux looked at her, somewhat taken aback, once again, he couldn’t help but realize what sort of existence she actually was.
The most knowledgeable being in the entire Multiverse.
"Then what do I do?"
He asked.
"You learn what I learned after clearing the Temple of Time and coming here.
The Law of Origin."

chapters.title: Chapter 2380: You are insane.
paragraphs: "You learn what I learned after I cleared the Temple of Time and came here.
The Law of Origin."
Nux stared at her.
For a moment, he said nothing, then he narrowed his eyes.
"Law of... Origin?"
The Seer nodded.
"Yes."
"That is the name of your Law?"
"Yes."
Nux looked at her for a while, then turned toward the endless Multiverse in front of him, then looked back at the Seer.
"For something that allows you to enter any Universe at any point in Time, the name is rather... simple."
"Simple things are often the... largest."
The Seer smiled.
"Is that so..."
Nux muttered as he continued to stare at her, waiting for an explanation.
"Every Universe has its own Time, its own flow, its own rhythm, its own direction. That is what separates one Universe from another."
"Yes, I know that."
Nux nodded.
The Seer nodded back, then she looked at him and—
"But that is not the complete truth."
Nux narrowed his eyes.
"Every Universe has a unique Time, that is correct, but no Universe’s Time was born from nothing."
The Seer then pointed at the Multiverse in front of her and started explaining.
"Every Universe here came from a Branch, every Branch came from another Universe, and all of them, no matter how distant, no matter how distorted, no matter how old, came from the First Universe."
"The Main Universe."
Nux mentioned.
"Yes."
The Seer nodded.
"The First Universe had the First Time.
The Original Time.
The beginning from which all other ’Times’ were born.
Every Branch changed it, every interference altered it, and all those changes... gave it a new Identity, a new Unique Time that later went on to become a Universe’s Identity."
Nux listened carefully, the Seer then turned towards him and—
"But beneath every variation, beneath every distortion, beneath every change...
The First Time still remained."
Nux noted those words with a new light in his eyes, still, he didn’t interrupt the Seer’s flow and let her continue.
"To ordinary beings, these Universes are separate existences with an entirely Unique Identity. To me—
They are countless variations of one Origin.
They may differ by a single breath, a war that never ended, a king that shouldn’t have perished, or a child who should have been born but wasn’t—
But all of them still carry the same base.
The same Origin.
The same mark of the Original Time, or the First Time."
The Seer then turned silent for a while, letting Nux absorb what she told him as she herself moved her gaze back to the Multiverse.
Then, once she noticed Nux was ready—
She continued.
"Every Universe has a Time Signature.

A unique identity formed from the Origin Time and all the changes that shaped it. I use my Law to read that signature, and once I read that Time Signature, I understand it and once I understand that Universe’s Time Signature—
I can enter any point within it.
The beginning, the end, or any event I desire."
Nux nodded as he tried to understand it all.
"So what you are saying is...
If we think of First Time as ’T’, then every Universe after it is T plus something, or T minus something, according to how much it has varied from the Original Timeline, correct?"
"Well, that is an extremely simplified version of it, but yes.
At some level, your assumption is correct."
The Seer nodded.
Nux nodded back, soon however, another question appeared in his head and he frowned.

"Knowing all the Time Signatures came from the First Time is one thing, how do you know how much a particular Universe’s Time Signature is different from the First Time? How do you know the exact identity of a particular Universe?
Like, you know every Universe is T plus something, or T minus something—
But how do you know that this particular Universe is... let’s say... T+23184?
What I am trying to ask is...
If I put you in front of nine vigintillion Universes—
How do you know which one is which?"
The Seer just smiled at that question.
"This is why I said your summarization was an extremely simplified version of reality, almost childishly so."
"I thought it was the easiest way to understand it."
Nux frowned.
"Well, it is the easiest, but at a deeper level—
It is also wrong."
Nux’s frown deepened.
"Time is not a number, Nux.
A Universe’s Time is not something you count from the outside.
It is a path.
A history that became an identity.
If you wish to know a Universe, you must know where it came from.
And if you wish to know where it came from—
You must trace it back to the beginning."
She explained.
Nux looked at her for what felt like a good few minutes and then—
"So that’s your Law?"
"That is the first step of it."
The Seer nodded.
"The first step?"
"Yes."
She turned towards him.
"The Law of Origin is simple.
To know anything, return it to its Origin.
To know a Universe, return it to the First Universe.
To know its Time, return it to the First Time."
Nux turned toward the Multiverse and looked at those endless branches.
"So you... trace every Universe back to the First Universe..."
"Yes."
"There are quindecillions of Branches between some of them."
He commented as he raised his eyebrow.
"Yes."
The Seer nodded like it was obvious.
Nux turned back towards her and—
"So you trace back through quindecillions of branches?"
"Yes."
"And you want me to do the same...?"
Nux asked, hoping she would say no but—
"Yes."
Nux just looked at the woman in front of him with a ridiculous look on his face.
"You are insane."
"I have been told that before."
"By whom?"
"Myself."
She laughed.
Nux stared at her, he had absolutely no clue what he was supposed to say here. The Seer, on the other hand, just shrugged.
Then she pointed at a pale blue branch far away and—
"Start there.
Trace that one back to the Single Root."
"You really are crazy."
Nux complained but—
"Stop complaining and get to work, Nux Leander."
The Seer just laughed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2381: What am I supposed to see?
paragraphs: "You really are crazy."
Nux complained but—
"Stop complaining and get to work, Nux Leander."
The Seer just laughed.
Nux looked at the branch, it stretched through the darkness, splitting from a larger silver branch, which itself split from another, which came from another, which came from another and so on...
Nux followed it with his gaze.
One branch to its parent.
Then to the parent of that parent.
Then farther back.
Then farther.
Then farther.
Then farther.
It was not difficult.
At least... not at first.
All he had to do was follow the line, the branch always came from somewhere, every Universe had a parent, every parent had its own parent, every line led back.
The problem was not difficulty.
The path... did not end.
Nux followed one split after another, hundreds, thousands... millions of them.
The branches became thicker the farther he went. Some parts of the path were buried under countless other branches, some were so bright that they blinded his sight.
Still, he followed them without problems.
Branch after branch, Universe after Universe, at this point, ordinary beings would have lost themselves.
But Nux was different.
His mind was far more developed even when compared to an Infinity, so he continued.
Time passed.
Or... something like time.
After all, time did not exist here, his mind only felt the weight of effort he was putting in.
He kept tracing back, at last, the branches grew fewer, then fewer, then fewer, until the path reached a massive, ancient stream of light.
And—
The instant he saw it—
He understood it.
This was it.
The First Universe.
The Main Universe.
The Origin of all Universes.
The first existence.
The Seer’s voice came from beside him.
"You found it."
The Seer, who had been silent all this while, commented with a light smile on her face. Nux didn’t move his eyes away from it, almost as if he was scared he would lose it.
The Seer’s smile widened when she noticed what he was thinking and—
"Now do it again."
She commanded.
And in an instant, Nux turned towards her with a surprised look on his face.
"What?"
She pointed toward a black branch as if nothing had happened and—
"Trace that one."
"You... aren’t kidding..."
"I am not."
The Seer shook her head.
"But I found the Root."
Nux frowned.
"Only once."
"Once is enough to understand the path."
"No."
The Seer shook her head.
"Once is enough to know that the path exists.
It is not enough tounderstandit.
Now get back to it."
She ordered, this time in a firmer tone. Nux looked at her for a moment, then he turned toward the new branch and began tracing it.
This one was longer.

Its path twisted through strange regions of the Multiverse. It came from a black branch, which came from a crimson one, which came from a silver one, which came from a dead-looking greyish branch and so on...
Nux followed the line as he moved further and further.
All the way until he reached the First Universe again.
"Again."

The Seer commanded and this time, Nux did not argue. Even though he couldn’t see how exactly repeating the same thing would help, he traced another Universe back to the First Universe like she told him to.
Then another.
Then another.
Then another.
At first, every path took time.
Some took years, or at least what felt like years.
Some even took centuries.

One had to understand that Nux’s mind was far quicker than a normal one, calculations that would take a normal mind days, months or even years to solve, Nux could complete them in an instant, even if he did not understand the concept behind them.

All he needed to do was look and his mind was so quick that it would first see the pattern, then find the concept inside that pattern, then find the solution to the particular problem he was presented—
All at the same time.
A menial task like finding branches was like a breeze for him, no matter how blinding the light was or how dense the network was—
Nux only needed a gaze.
Then why did it take so long?
It was because of the sheer number of branches he needed to go through. This was also the reason Nux complained so much at first, more than understanding, this felt like thankless labour.
But Nux did it anyways.
Every time he reached the First Universe, the Seer gave him another branch.
Again.
Again.
And again.
And with time—
Nux became faster.

His mind had once again started realizing patterns, this time, at a bigger level than before, some branches split in similar ways, some regions of the Multiverse had common flows, some lineages carried certain shapes, some ancient trunks always led toward the same deeper paths.
Nux’s mind noted it all, then it adjusted.
A path that once took years began taking months.
Then days.
Then moments.
Then he could look at a branch and trace its outer lineage back to the Single Root almost instantly.
The Seer watched him and for the first time, she nodded.
"Good."
Nux glanced at her.
"That’s all?"
He asked.
The Seer laughed at that question.
"You learned the first step."
"It took me years..."
Nux spoke in a low tone.
"Don’t worry, the Multiverse doesn’t count."
She chuckled, then, she pointed toward the branches again and—
"All this time, you were looking at the branches."
"Yes."
Nux nodded.
He had looked so much that he was sick at this point.
What he didn’t know was that this was the easiest part.
There was far worse coming.
"Now look at the Universes."
The Seer directed.
Nux frowned.
"I thought the brancheswereUniverses."
"They are."
"Then what are you talking about?"
The Seer looked at him and—
"What you are seeing is just the Universe’s outer body, its depiction in the Multiverse.
Now I want you to lookinsidethe Universe."
"...what?"
Nux blinked. He turned toward the closest branch. A silver and blue flowing quietly through the dark.
To him, that was all it looked like, a beautiful stream of light.
He focused on it and...
Nothing changed.
"It is still a branch."
He commented.
"No. You are still onlyseeinga branch."
Nux’s eyebrow twitched.
"You are very fond of saying things like that."
"And you are very fond of being wrong."
Nux slowly turned toward her.
The Seer kept staring at him with that same smile on her face.
For a moment, Nux wanted to punch her, but then he sighed and looked back at the branch.
"What am I supposed to see?"
He asked with a defeated look on his face.

chapters.title: Chapter 2382: How do you do it?
paragraphs: "What am I supposed to see?"
Nux asked with a defeated look on his face.
"Everything."
The Seer answered.
Nux frowned in confusion and the Seer started explaining.

"A branch is not merely a line, Nux. It is a Universe seen from outside Time. It is the beginning, it is the past, it is the present, it is the future, its Laws, its worlds, its deaths, its wars, its Branches and... it is the end.
Everything that makes a Universe a... Universe exists inside that one stream."
Nux blinked.
"You see all of that at once...?"
He asked in disbelief.
"Yes."
"And you expect me to do the same...?"
"Yes."
The Seer nodded again.
Nux stared at the branch again.
For now, he finally understood why the Seer said the first step was easy, tracing the outside of a branch was simple, this was... something else.
He focused.
The silver-blue branch shined but—
Nothing happened.
Nux went at it for days, days turned into months, then years and centuries but...
He found himself seeing just the branch.
"How do you do it?"
He asked with a deep frown.
"No matter how much I keep staring, I only see a branch."
"That is for you to figure out."
The Seer had no answer.
"How doyoudo it?"
He asked.
"I just... do?"
The Seer tilted her head and she wasn’t lying, to her, all this came naturally when she came here.
Nux’s mouth twitched.
"You are a terrible teacher."
"I agree."
The Seer nodded and that only made it worse.
In the end, Nux just turned towards the branch and looked.
But again, it didn’t change anything. It was almost as if seeing what the Seer saw was impossi—
Suddenly, Nux’s thoughts froze.
Impossible.
Seeing what the Seer saw was impossible!
Why didn’t he think of that before!?
He cursed himself for restricting himself to what he was being told, then—
He cheated.
The Power of Anomaly moved, Nux’s eyes brightened and now, as he looked at the Universe with the intent tolook—
It happened.
Something opened and Nux’s mind was struck with an overwhelming stream of information, all at once.
Stars.
Worlds.
Births.
Deaths.
Wars.
Civilizations.
Immortals.
Mortals.
Children.
Monsters.
Laws.
Oceans.
Screams.
Silence.
Fire.
Time.
All of it came.
Everything came at once, not one event after another, not past, then present, then future.
All of itcame together.
The birth of the Universe and its final decay, a child’s first breath and an ancient star’s death, it all... coexisted.
A war that lasted ten thousand years existed beside the thought that caused it. An Immortal’s rise, fall, return, and erasure all appeared as one structure.
Nux’s consciousness shook.
For a moment, he almost lost himself.
It was too much, even for him, who had absorbed Worlds’ worth of memories.
After all, this was not mere worlds.
It was a complete Universe.
A whole Universe’s existence, compressed into one sight.
Nux had to use all his will, all his power, just to keep his mind intact and keep his sense of self.

He constantly remembered his wives, his children, everything that was important to him, his goal to return, his goal to meet his wives again, the agony they must be in, the tears they must have shed when they saw that recording he left, he remembered it all and slowly—
His will became stronger than the information he received and finally—
It stayed.
He remained... himself.
And he...
He closed his eyes and took deep breaths even when the concept of breathing didn’t exist here.
"You finally saw it."
The Seer commented.
"...a little heads up would have been great."
Nux answered after about ten minutes of silence and keeping his mind intact. The loud thumping in his head was finally over, that feeling that he was about to lose himself finally disappeared.
"Heads up about what?"
The Seer tilted her head.
"That the moment I actually do look at the Universe, the information might overwhelm my mind and I might lose my sense of self if I am not careful."
"...was that not... obvious?"
The Seer frowned.
"You are looking at the Universe, from its beginning to the end, that is at least a decillion years’ worth of information, what did you think would happen?"
She asked and Nux...
He just looked away.
What could he even say?
"What do I do now?"
So in the end, he did what he did best, he changed the topic.
"Look again and process that information."
"Process it...?"
"Of course, you onlysawthat information, how much of it do you recall?"
"It was chaotic, not something thatcouldbe recalled."
Nux answered.
"You are wrong.
Do it again."
The Seer ordered and Nux...
He prepared himself and looked at the Universe again, the information struck again, trying to overwhelm his mind again, but this time, he held on and handled it much better.
Then—
His mind tried to make sense of it.
First, he tried to separate it.
The Beginning.
The Middle.
The End.
He tried to create a timeline that would make sense.
But it failed.
Nux frowned, he thought of trying it again but—
"Order belongs inside Time."
The Seer spoke up.
Nux didn’t stop looking into the Universe, but his mind had shifted its attention to her words.
"But you are not inside Time.
You are in the Multiverse.
The Universe you see is not a story being told.
It is a complete thing.
A finished and unfinished thing at the same time.
A body made of moments.
Do not try to force it into order, take it all at once, like it is being presented."
Nux understood those words and this time, he used a newer approach.
He started looking at the small parts first.
A single, simplest form of life.
He saw its past, present, future, everything its little life entailed at once and he understood it. Then from there, he began focusing on larger parts.
A comparatively bigger but simple life form.
Then a more complex life form.
Then multiple life forms.
Then an entire continent.
An entire civilization.
An entire World.
Multiple Worlds.

Then slowly and steadily, as his mind got used to the overwhelming amount of information it was subjected to, as it was broken again and again, barely holding on only by a small, but ridiculously strong Will—
He could finally see it.
He could finally... understand it.
But—
Just as he was about to celebrate.
"Now trace it back."
"...what?"

Something opened and Nux’s mind was struck with an overwhelming stream of information, all at once.
Stars.
Worlds.
Births.
Deaths.
Wars.
Civilizations.
Immortals.
Mortals.
Children.
Monsters.
Laws.
Oceans.
Screams.
Silence.
Fire.
Time.
All of it came.
Everything came at once, not one event after another, not past, then present, then future.
All of itcame together.
The birth of the Universe and its final decay, a child’s first breath and an ancient star’s death, it all... coexisted.
A war that lasted ten thousand years existed beside the thought that caused it.
An Immortal’s rise, fall, return, and erasure all appeared as one structure.
Nux’s consciousness shook.
For a moment, he almost lost himself.
It was too much, even for him, who had absorbed Worlds’ worth of memories.
After all, this was not mere worlds.
It was a complete Universe.
A whole Universe’s existence, compressed into one sight.
Nux had to use all his will, all his power, just to keep his mind intact and keep his sense of self.

He constantly remembered his wives, his children, everything that was important to him, his goal to return, his goal to meet his wives again, the agony they must be in, the tears they must have shed when they saw that recording he left, he remembered it all and slowly—
His will became stronger than the information he received and finally—
It stayed.
He remained... himself.
And he...
He closed his eyes and took deep breaths even when the concept of breathing didn’t exist here.
"You finally saw it."
The Seer commented.
"...a little heads up would have been great."
Nux answered after about ten minutes of silence and keeping his mind intact.
The loud thumping in his head was finally over, that feeling that he was about to lose himself finally disappeared.
"Heads up about what?"
The Seer tilted her head.
"That the moment I actually do look at the Universe, the information might overwhelm my mind and I might lose my sense of self if I am not careful."
"...was that not... obvious?"
The Seer frowned.
"You are looking at the Universe, from its beginning to the end, that is at least a decillion years’ worth of information, what did you think would happen?"
She asked and Nux...
He just looked away.
What could he even say?
"What do I do now?"
So in the end, he did what he did best, he changed the topic.
"Look again and process that information."
"Process it...?"
"Of course, you onlysawthat information, how much of it do you recall?"
"It was chaotic, not something thatcouldbe recalled."
Nux answered.
"You are wrong.
Do it again."
The Seer ordered and Nux...
He prepared himself and looked at the Universe again, the information struck again, trying to overwhelm his mind again, but this time, he held on and handled it much better.
Then—
His mind tried to make sense of it.
First, he tried to separate it.
The Beginning.
The Middle.
The End.
He tried to create a timeline that would make sense.
But it failed.
Nux frowned, he thought of trying it again but—
"Order belongs inside Time."
The Seer spoke up.
Nux didn’t stop looking into the Universe, but his mind had shifted its attention to her words.
"But you are not inside Time.
You are in the Multiverse.
The Universe you see is not a story being told.
It is a complete thing.
A finished and unfinished thing at the same time.
A body made of moments.
Do not try to force it into order, take it all at once, like it is being presented."
Nux understood those words and this time, he used a newer approach.
He started looking at the small parts first.
A single, simplest form of life.
He saw its past, present, future, everything its little life entailed at once and he understood it.
Then from there, he began focusing on larger parts.
A comparatively bigger but simple life form.
Then a more complex life form.
Then multiple life forms.
Then an entire continent.
An entire civilization.
An entire World.
Multiple Worlds.

Then slowly and steadily, as his mind got used to the overwhelming amount of information it was subjected to, as it was broken again and again, barely holding on only by a small, but ridiculously strong Will—
He could finally see it.
He could finally... understand it.
But—
Just as he was about to celebrate.
"Now trace it back."
"...what?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2383: The First Universe.
paragraphs: "Now trace it back."
The Seer commanded and Nux looked at her like he was seeing his worst enemy.
"...what?
I already traced this branch back to the First Universe."
"You said it yourself, you traced the branch.
Now trace the Universe."
The Seer spoke with a serious look on her face and Nux...
He gulped.
He didn’t need to be a genius to know how nightmarish what she was saying was.
"Every branch is born because ’Time’ was disturbed.
If you truly wish to know the Universe, merely following its outer connection to its root is not enough.
You need to look inside and find the exact incidents that created the Branch.
The moments Time split and gave birth to the Universe as you are seeing it, all while you trace those moments back to the Main Universe."
Nux didn’t say anything.
He wanted to complain but he too knew how important it was, so instead of using his energy to complain, he worked.
He looked inside the silver-blue Universe again.
And again, it was madness.

A whole Universe’s past, present, and future pressed into his mind, countless events called to him, every war looked important, every death had consequences, every birth led somewhere, every use of power left marks, every Law changed something—
But not all changes created Branches.
So he ignored those and focused on those that did.

At first, it was difficult, searching through that endless stream of information. According to him, it took him at least a million years of constantly breaking his mind again and again to finally be able to take the information and not be at risk of losing his sense of self.
But now...
To search through this information—
It wasn’t an easy task.
But he did it anyways.
He searched through the complete structure and—
There.

Nux paused, his eyes noticing a being standing at the edge of a dying world. The people of this world had already died, the sky had collapsed, the Universe was moving towards a future where that world returned to nothingness.
But—
The being used the Power of Time to send one simple memory into the past, that was all he had the power to do—
And that was enough.
A Branch formed.

The past changed, the world prepared, its inevitable collapse was delayed, that delay caused another being to survive, that survival changed the course of a war, and that war changed the fate of a Universe itself.
The original future could no longer remain the only path and—
The Branch turned into a full-fledged Universe.
That was it.
That was the birth of the silver-blue Universe.
That was what separated it from its parent, the Pale Blue Universe.
"There it is."
Nux pointed at it, he didn’t know if the Seer would be able to see it but—
"Yes."
She nodded.
"Now find the birth of the Pale Blue Universe."
She commanded.
Nux expected it and he did what he was told.
The Pale Blue Universe came from a Dark Blue Universe, Nux found the exact incident that happened, then, according to the Seer’s instruction, he did the same with the Dark Blue Universe.
Then with the Universe that was parent to the Dark Blue Universe.
Then the Parent’s Parent.
The Parent’s Parent’s Parent.
And so on...
All the way back to the First Universe.
This was far, far more difficult than tracing just the outer branch, the outer branch was merely a depiction, a path, whereas the Inner Universe was... everything.
Nux had to look at an entire Universe, find the one event that mattered, then use that event to move backward through its lineage.
It was... no different than mental torture.
He was wrong more times than he could even keep count.
He thought a war had created the Branch, but the Seer showed him that the true cause was one child who was saved two thousand years before the war.
He thought a Transcendent’s death had created the Branch, but the true cause was the said Transcendent seeing his death in the future and changing one decision centuries earlier.

Actually, after that first fluke, Nux was wrong almost every other time. The Seer had to correct him again and again, it was basically just the Seer doing the work while Nux did everything in his power to follow along.
Still—
After what felt like trillions of years had passed, after Nux could look at the Universe without feeling even the slightest pain in his head, he started to change.
His understanding of a Universe itself strengthened to another level.
It made him a different person than he was before.
With time, his eyes felt... different.
They felt more... distant.
"Do not lose yourself in the Multiverse. That would ruin the entire point of what you are doing."
The Seer warned when she noticed that.
"I know."
Nux nodded, but the distant look in his eyes did not change.
The Seer narrowed her eyes.
"Do not absorb a Universe’s memory, you will overwhelm your mind if you do that. Read it, find what you want, discard the rest and move along.
Do not burden your mind more than you have to."
She advised.
"I understand that."
Nux nodded and the Seer... she didn’t say anything else and decided to do what she had been doing all this while—
To trust that he would pull himself through.
Just like that—
More time passed, and the more he practiced, the better Nux got.
He learned that Time was cruelly delicate, a Branch did not always form from the largest event, sometimes, the largest event was only the shadow of a tiny disturbance.
He learned that every Universe had a Birth Wound—an event that branched Time.
And every Wound had a shape.
Nux learned those shapes.
The more Nux saw, the faster he became.
But...
The path was still enormous.
One Universe could have quindecillions of ancestors. To trace it back properly, Nux had to enter the sight of one Universe, find its Birth Wound, follow it to the parent, then repeat.
Again and again and again.
For years that he had long stopped counting.
And finally—
He had traced a silver-blue Universe back through an impossible line of ancestors, until there were no more Birth Wounds, no more branches to read—
The First Universe.
He had succeeded.
But then—
"Now do it again with that Universe."

chapters.title: Chapter 2384: I am fine.
paragraphs: Nux had traced a silver-blue Universe back through an impossible line of ancestors, until there were no more Birth Wounds, no more branches to read—
The First Universe.
He had succeeded.
But then—
"Now do it again with that Universe."
The Seer commanded.
Nux looked at her for a short moment, then he looked at the Universe she pointed at and did what he was told.
Once again, he moved through the complete lineage of the Universe, through different branches of Time, until he returned to the constant—
To the First Time.
Then he did it again.
And again.
And again.

So many times until his mind got used to it, to seeing the Universe’s structure, to finding the ’Birth Wound’ in an instant, to moving through that Wound, through that branch, and repeating the entire thing with the next Parent Universe without getting tired.
"Now do the opposite."
The Seer commanded.
Nux turned towards her with almost no expression on his face, waiting for her to explain. At this point, the Seer was used to that gaze, so she simply pointed towards a distant branch and—
"Start from the First Universe, follow the Branches forward, and get to that Universe."
Nux understood instantly.
The first half was tracing back and this...
This was worse.
After all, while tracing back, he only had to remove the changes until only the Origin remained.
But this...
This meant he needed to build Time’s identity step by step, all the way from the First Time, through every disturbance, every deviation, every altered future, to finally the target Universe.
"So this is how you know.
You do not guess the Time of a Universe, you reconstruct it."
Nux commented in a disturbingly calm tone.
"Yes."
In her mind, the Seer preferred the version where he was still complaining about the work she was making him do but—
She too understood what he had been through, to go through quindecillions of Universes’ memories, again and again, even if the mind abandoned most of it—
It would still be taxing.
It would still... affect him in some way.
There was nothing she could do about it.
She just convinced herself that he would return to normal oncethathappened.
Nux, on the other hand, shifted his focus to the target Universe, then back to the First Universe.
And he began.
From the First Time, he moved forward, the First Branch.
He looked inside it, he saw the first time ’Time’ was disturbed enough to split reality, the first time the Single Root could no longer remain alone.
Nux studied it.
The deviation formed, he followed it, then the next Branch, then another, and then another—

The path grew longer, each ’Wound’ changed the flow, each flow changed the next Wound, some deviations strengthened each other, some cancelled parts of each other, some twisted the entire path, some left marks that only mattered quindecillions of Branches later—
And Nux—
He had to remember all of it.
He had to carry every change from the First Universe, all the way to the target.
And again—
Even as he focused,

He failed before reaching even a tiny fraction of the path, his consciousness became overloaded, he lost track of one branch, then the other, the Identity of the Time he had been trying to preserve in his head lost its meaning, forcing him to start again.
So he did.
He started again.
Then he failed again.
Started.
Failed.
Started.
Failed.
The Seer watched as he continued repeating the cycle without uttering even a single word, like a machine that wouldn’t stop the iterations until it was successful.
And...
It worried her.
She could feel that Nux was losing himself.
But—
Every time she called him out like this,
"I am fine.
I am not losing myself.
Do not worry."
Nux said those words and as unconvincing as those words sounded, for some reason, the Seer believed them every single time and—
"Okay..."
She nodded and continued to watch as she stood beside him for... who knows how many years.
Nux repeated the cycle again and again, until his speed grew, until his mind started to catch the patterns.

He learned to group certain deviations, he learned to recognize common chains, he learned how one type of Time disturbance affected another, he learned which events had long-lasting weight that he should note and which faded into the flow that he could ignore.
He learned which changes looked small but altered everything, he learned which changes looked massive but changed almost nothing.
The Multiverse became less like a forest of light and more like... a language.
A language Nux was beginning to understand.
The Branches, the Universes, the Birth Wounds, the First Universe, the First Time, the Origin, the Identity of a Universe, how the Identity of a Universe is affected by a specific event—
It all started to make sense in his mind.
And finally—
He succeeded.
He traced the target Universe all the way from the First Universe.
And as he looked at the Seer standing in front of him—
"Give me the next Universe."
He demanded.
She hesitated.
The Seer wanted him to take some rest, to give his mind time to return to his normal self before it was too late.
But—
"I am fine."
Nux spoke as he read her expression and in the end, she gave in and pointed at another Universe.
Nux began tracing it forward without any change in his expression.
Millions of years passed again.
And finally, when Nux was done, he looked at the Seer again and asked for another target Universe.
The Seer gave in again, she pointed at the Universe, Nux traced it forward, then he asked for more, she gave him another.
Then another.
Another.
One more.
At first, it took millions of years to calculate one.
And for the Seer, that was enough, that was all Nux needed to understand how her Law worked, so she wanted him to stop.
But he didn’t.
He practiced.
He did the same thing again and again.
And then—
The time he needed began to decrease.
First, it came down to a few hundred thousand years.
Then just thousands.
Then a few decades.
A few years.
And the Seer’s expression began to change.
At first, she was watching him like he was a child learning to walk, then he became a student who was growing—
But—
The more she watched him, the more silent she grew.
Because Nux was no longer ’following’ paths, he was...
He was predicting them.
And the Seer couldn’t believe it.

chapters.title: Chapter 2385: Thank you for the gift.
paragraphs: The more she watched him, the more silent she grew.
Because Nux was no longer ’following’ paths, he was...
He was predicting them.

If a Universe carried a certain kind of scar, its lineage often bent in a certain direction that he could predict. If its flow had a certain weight, it likely passed through certain ancient Branches that he could completely skip and move right past. If its Time had certain fractures, it had likely inherited them from a specific class of disturbance.
Nux had learned all those patterns, patterns that... she only learned after watching the Multiverse for quindecillions of years.
What the Seer did not realize was that—
As exceptional of a being as she, or more accurately, her past incarnation was before she came to the Multiverse—
Nux Leander stood at an entirely different level.

Sure, both Avernyth and Vashti were exceptional. One was the Infinity of Eternity, an Infinity with such a great impact on the Universe that even to this day, even when she had been erased, the Universe still remembers her. The other was the only being who cleared the Temple of Trials.
But Nux?

He was no normal being, he couldn’t even be judged as one. He not only cleared the Temple of Time like Vashti did, hebrokeit and created a completely different concept of Time that had no relationship with the Multiverse’s Original Time whatsoever.
And that wasjustTime.
Nux had mastered every single Primordial Energy, he was a literal Universe. A being whose very mind was built for devouring systems, breaking them, and turning them into weapons he could use.
And the Law of Origin was no different.
Nux had devoured it too.
So the moment the Seer pointed at a specific Universe and asked him to—
"Trace that one."
Nux looked at it and the next second—
"It came from the gray-gold trunk near the eastern flow."
He had the answer.

"Before that, it passed through a dead Branch that survived because its future was stolen and planted into its own past. Before that, a crimson Universe born from a war that shouldn’t have happened. Before that, a blue Branch created when a Time Beast devoured the same year seven times..."
The story continued, all the way till the First Universe. Nux skipped more than a few details because he knew the Seer would catch on and finally—
"Its Time is unstable at the beginning, clean in the middle, and rotting near the end. That is what causes it to decay before it should have."
"Correct."
The Seer nodded.
"You have reached my level."
She admitted it.
Nux remained silent for a while, as if he was thinking about something. Then, he looked at her and—
"Now to enter a specific Universe, you simply align yourself with its Time Signature and that grants you entrance, correct?"
He asked. His mind had already understood the Law of Origin, so there was nothing more the Seer could teach him.
"Yes."
She could only nod.
"But even now, even at the level you are in—
You can never entermyUniverse, even as an observer, because you never managed to learn its Time Signature."
"Your Universe isn’t connected to the Origin Time, I have no way to learn its Time Signature."
She admitted.
"This is why all this while, every time you interacted with me, you never actually knew what was going to happen, you just predicted the possible future after analysing all the key players involved."
"That is correct."
"You worked hard."
Nux praised.
The Seer just smiled.
Nux just looked at her with that same distant look on his face, then—
"But even you have no idea how to proceed from this point onwards, do you?"
That made the Seer pause for a moment. She looked into Nux’s eyes, trying to find even a hint of emotion, but she couldn’t find any.
There was no anger, no disappointment, neither was there any amusement or excitement.
"I gave you everything I have."
In the end, the Seer just lowered her head, indirectly admitting it.
Thiswas the Third Gift.
The Law of Origin.
A Power to enter any Universe, at any point in Time, throughout the Multiverse.
Now...
As to what Nux would do with this power, or what Nuxcoulddo with this power to improve his situation—
She had no clue.
All this while, she only trusted him to find a way out of the impossible-to-escape cage she was in because...
That was what Nux always did.
The Impossible.
And right now was no different.
Because as Nux stared at the woman in front of him—
"You did well."
He praised.
Then, he bowed his head.
"Thank you for the gift."
The Seer’s expression changed the moment she heard those words.
Relief.
A wave of strong relief hit her.

She had been holding it in for hundreds of millions of years Nux had been here. She had been trying to keep a strong front, all while wondering if Nux would ever accept her gift but now that he had...
"Thank you..."
She muttered.
And for the first time ever since she became the Seer, a drop of tear rolled down her blindfold.
Nux gently wiped her tears.
None of them had physical bodies, in fact, none of them even had a Soul, they were merely... a consciousness, an amalgamation of thoughts.
Thoughts so powerful and vast that they alone had given them what looked like a physical body.
"...what are you going to do now?"
The Seer asked as she looked into Nux’s eyes, which were still distant. It was almost as if his eyes had memorized that shape.
Nux looked at her, then finally, his eyes reflected a different emotion.
Excitement.
Eagerness.
And...
Intense, almost violent longing.
"I will return to my wives."
He spoke.
The Seer looked at him in silence, her eyes still hidden behind her blindfold, so it was next to impossible for any being to know what she was feeling.
But Nux was different.
He could sense her disappointment.
And he—
"I will return to my Universe.
With you."
He gave a proper, complete answer as he gently held her hand.

Nux had learned all those patterns, patterns that... she only learned after watching the Multiverse for quindecillions of years.

As exceptional of a being as she, or more accurately, her past incarnation was before she came to the Multiverse—
Nux Leander stood at an entirely different level.
Sure, both Avernyth and Vashti were exceptional.

Nux had devoured it too.

chapters.title: Chapter 2386: Absolute Emptiness.
paragraphs: In a grand room larger than most royal halls, there was a giant bed at the very centre and on that bed, there lay 24 children, all sleeping peacefully, with carefree looks on their faces.
They were Nux’s children, blissfully unaware of what had happened.
Their mothers, on the other hand, were entirely different. Unlike the peaceful, carefree expressions on the children’s faces, the mothers’ faces only showed...
Emptiness.
Absolute Emptiness.

Most of them didn’t even want to be here, after everything had happened, they didn’t even wish to exist, every single one of them wanted to follow Nux to death and the only reason they hadn’t was because...
These children lying on the bed.
Nux’s last wish.
He wanted them to be there for their children, they had already lost their father, he didn’t wish for them to lose their mothers too.
The women were no different either, as they watched their children sleep, they too, didn’t have the heart to leave them, no matter how desperately they wanted to.
So...
They sought the only form of slight comfort they could.
Their children still had Nux’s eyes, Nux’s smile, Nux’s stubbornness, Nux’s warmth, little pieces of him hidden inside their faces—
They observed that, they recalled every memory they had of him and... they kept themselves sane.
Barely.
Felberta sat near the head of the bed, she hadn’t moved for a long time, her hand rested on Lysera’s hair, gently stroking it with a lost look on her face.
Her eyes were red, her face was pale, her tears had dried on her cheeks long ago, but new ones still gathered in her eyes, her usual steadiness, her usual composure was nowhere to be seen.
Her mind was constantly replaying the memory of the first time she met him, the first time he came to her, the first time they talked, the first time he tricked her...
Everything.
Her mind replayed everything as the tears that welled in her eyes streamed down.
Skyla sat on the floor near the bed, her back resting against its side, her knees pulled to her chest.

Seeing her usual cheerfulness now completely gone was... devastating. Even the one who smiled all the time and kept everyone together with her cheerfulness was currently dead silent, she herself was too big of a mess to take care of anyone else.

Her eyes were swollen, her hair was messy, falling over her face as she stared at nothing. Every now and then, her lips trembled as if she was resisting the urge to cry. Time and time again, she looked at her children, trying to ease her heart, but it wasn’t working.
Lane had it the worst.
She was near the shadows under the bed, her form barely visible, she looked like a girl who had lost her home and now didn’t belong anywhere.
And in some sense—
She truly was homeless.
After all, for her, Nux’s Shadow was her home, the place she felt the safest, the one place where she could always feel him.
But now—
That Shadow was gone.

And Lane looked like a person who had been thrown out of her own existence. Her body trembled softly, her thin, shadowy hand slowly reached out from the darkness and held the corner of the bedsheet, gripping it so tightly that the cloth had begun to tear.
Shadow saw her state and for the first time—
She couldn’t come up with anything snarky to tease her. She just... stood near the wall, staring at... nothing.
She was no longer the Goddess of the Universe, she was now the Absolute, the being who held all the power here.
A power that would corrupt most beings in existence.
But Shadow?
She hated every bit of this power.
Heck, she hated her very being. After all, if she wasn’t who she was, Nux would have never been able to make her inherit the Universe.
And if he had no one to inherit the Universe, if he knew his death would mean his wives’ deaths, he would have been much much much more careful.
He wouldn’t have died.
No matter what—
He wouldn’t have died.
The only reason he died was because of her and for that—
Shadow would never forgive herself.
And while Shadow was drowning in self-hatred, frustration and helplessness, Edda was sitting at the edge of the bed, holding Veyron’s little hand with both of hers.

Her usual warmth was gone, her friendly smile was gone, even the shameless, perverted thoughts that usually filled her mind when she thought of Nux had disappeared, crushed beneath a grief so heavy it had left no space for anything else.
"He has his fingers..."
She muttered in a broken voice as she lowered her head and kissed her son’s hand.
And the instant she did that—
Tears streamed down her cheeks.
Allura, who was sitting beside her, patted her shoulder.
The Succubus’s eyes were wet, but her face was... strangely calm.
Too calm.
If Nux had seen her like this, it would have broken him.
Because this wasn’t Allura ’handling’ herself, it was her after she had cried until her sense of ’self’ had somewhat disappeared.
Her current self was nothing more than a hollow puppet who was only moving because she had to move.
As for her mind—
It had already collapsed.
Thyra crouched near the foot of the bed, her ears were lowered, her tail lay behind her lifelessly, her fingers were curled against the floor, her claws had dug into the floor.
Every few moments, her eyes moved toward the door, then the window, then the ceiling and then the shadows, as if she was looking for something...
Or... someone.
She was waiting for Nux to return.
Even when she knew he wouldn’t, she... she was still waiting helplessly because that was the only way her mind wouldn’t collapse.
Then, there was Amaya.
The Devourer was standing near the largest window with an absolutely calm look on her face, almost as if everything that had happened hadn’t fazed her, not one bit.
Or at least—
That was what it would look like to others who didn’t know her.
As for those who did...?
That was different.

chapters.title: Chapter 2387: Helplessness.
paragraphs: The Devourer was standing near the largest window with an absolutely calm look on her face, almost as if everything that had happened hadn’t fazed her, not one bit.
Or at least—
That was what it would look like to others who didn’t know her.
As for those who did...?
That was different.
Like Allura, Amaya no longer had tears to shed, however, unlike Allura whose mind had collapsed, Amaya’s mind had attached itself to something else.
Something... more terrifying.
Revenge.
She stared into the window’s glass as if she could see the Infinities beyond it.
Her fingers were wrapped around her own arms so tightly that her nails had cut into her skin, blood had already stained her sleeves, but she did not seem to feel it.
Her mind hadn’t stopped working.
Even now.
Especiallynow.
Nux had made it almost impossible for them to take revenge, almost.
But Amaya found a way out.
Or at least, a possible way out.
Zylarith Chaosveil.
Before dying, Nux devoured his existence, all she needed to do was use Shadow and get Zylarith’s memories from her.
Then, she would create the Cultivation Bridge that would lead them all the way to the Infinity Stage.
Then, she wouldbecomean Infinity and force her way out of the Universe.
Then—
She would kill every last one of them.
As painfully as possible.
Her eyes burned as the darkness in them became stronger than ever.

Riona, who was standing nearby, trembled when she saw the look on her daughter’s face. Riona’s case was worse than the others, she didn’t just have to bear with the loss of the husband she dearly loved, she also saw her daughter’s state, her anger and...
It scared her.
It scared her to even think about what would happen if all the anger boiling inside Amaya found no direction.
In the end, the only thing she could do was place her hand on her daughter’s shoulder, hoping to calm her down and at the same time... seek some form of relief for herself.
It didn’t work.
Her heart only felt heavier.
And Amaya...
"Mother... I cannot breathe."
The Devourer spoke as her body shook. Riona’s body trembled at those words and she pulled Amaya into her arms, as if scared she would lose her too.
And—
The mother-daughter pair, the pair that had always kept a straight head, the pair that had come up with strategies normal beings wouldn’t even be able to imagine—
They burst into tears.
Ember, standing near one of the pillars, watched them in silence.

Her body was still, as if she had forgotten how to move. When she first saw everything that was happening to Nux, how the Infinities had surrounded him, how the Seer had betrayed him, all she felt was rage, unbearable, uncontrollable rage.
Her very soul demanded blood.
It cried, wanting to be sent in front of the Infinities so she could tear them apart but...
She couldn’t leave.
She couldn’t help Nux and because of that—
He died.
He died fighting his enemies alone.
And...
That made her feel something worse than rage.
Helplessness.
Tears streamed down her cheeks while her expression stayed hard, her hands clenched into fists, the pillar beside her had cracks in it and she...
She could only stare at her children and... hold herself back...
Opposite Ember was Evane, who was sitting beside Eloria and the other children, her hands moving softly, fixing blankets, touching foreheads, calming the small restless movements of sleeping bodies.
Even now, the woman was gentle.
Even when her own heart had been crushed into pieces, she looked... stronger than most women in the room.
She took care of all the children because she knew their mothers were not in the state to.
Kira, Thyra’s daughter, whimpered in her sleep, Evane immediately leaned forward and hummed softly, calming her down.
Evane smiled.
It was a small, broken smile.
And when she could no longer hold back, she turned away before the children or any of her sisters could see the tears in her eyes.

Astaria stood with a sword in her hand, staring at it with a lost look on her face. Her mind continued to recall all the times she had challenged him, all the times he defeated her with that cheeky smile on his face, all the times he used their battle as an excuse to make his perverted moves on her and—
Her hand tightened around the sword’s hilt before she dropped it on the floor.
Yes, Astaria Leander was abandoning her sword.
After all, what good was her sword when she wasn’t even strong enough to fight next to him?
Vyriana, who was standing right next to her, was no different. The proud look on her face was gone and was replaced by... guilt and helplessness.
Vyriana had always prided herself on being a warrior, a being who never backed away from a fight.
Heh.
How laughable.
When she was most needed, when her husband was surrounded by the five strongest beings in the Universe and was fighting them alone—
All she could do was watch.
AWarriorindeed.
Vyriana laughed at herself, then she made a decision.
She would no longer fight.
Because like Astaria, she too, did not deserve it.
While both warriors made heart-breaking decisions, Aisha was sitting on the bed, cupping Velora’s cheeks with shaking hands.

Her usually bold, passionate self looked broken, her lips trembled. She thought about how she used to cling to Nux, tease, kiss, claim him openly, even in front of the children and how every time she did it—
Nux accepted it with a smile and looked at her with eyes filled with that strong, intense love.
That memory put a smile on her face.
But—
The moment reality dawned in—
The moment she realized how Nux was no longer there to cling to, Aisha bent forward and pressed her forehead against the blanket, trying to hide her tears.

Heh.
How laughable.
When she was most needed, when her husband was surrounded by the five strongest beings in the Universe and was fighting them alone—
All she could do was watch.
AWarriorindeed.
Vyriana laughed at herself, then she made a decision.
She would no longer fight.
Because like Astaria, she too, did not deserve it.
While both warriors made heart-breaking decisions, Aisha was sitting on the bed, cupping Velora’s cheeks with shaking hands.
Her usually bold, passionate self looked broken, her lips trembled.
She thought about how she used to cling to Nux, tease, kiss, claim him openly, even in front of the children and how every time she did it—
Nux accepted it with a smile and looked at her with eyes filled with that strong, intense love.
That memory put a smile on her face.
But—
The moment reality dawned in—
The moment she realized how Nux was no longer there to cling to, Aisha bent forward and pressed her forehead against the blanket, trying to hide her tears.

chapters.title: Chapter 2388: Nux...?
paragraphs: Melia sat on a chair near the side of the room, with a straight, elegant posture, her hands rested in her lap and she...
She did not move an inch.
Tears kept pouring down her eyes, but she didn’t wipe them even once. She looked like a statue made from absolute grief.
A woman whose mind had collapsed entirely.
Aeliana was standing right beside her, her eyes were fixed on the sleeping children, her pale face was even paler.
There was no other expression on her face.
In some way, she looked better than the rest of the women present here, that was until one realized the fact that Aeliana was no longer saying a word.
[Aeliana... talk to me...]
Azriel had been trying to converse with her since the moment it all began but the moment Aeliana registered Nux’s death—
Her mind shut down.

She didn’t even bother disconnecting the call with her father, she just... remained still... no longer reacting to anything that was happening around her and that scared Azriel more than anything else in the Universe.
[Aeliana!!]
He continued to call her, to get to her just one time, but it didn’t work.
Lyriana, who was standing near Evane with one hand resting on the bedpost saw him, she saw how one of the strongest beings in the Universe was completely helpless right now but—
She didn’t react to it.
Or more like—
Her mind didn’t register it.
Her mind had locked itself inside the same memory, the memory when Nux claimed her and took her with him.
That was all she thought about.
That was all she wanted to think about.
Eisheth was no different, her thoughts had frozen too, her mind simply refused to admit what had happened, it didn’t even register the past few hours, as if all of it was an illusion.
The Succubus was simply looking at her sleeping daughter and closed her eyes while she sat next to her.
She would sleep too.
And once she woke up—
He would be here.
She knew it.
She knew it for sure.
She knew because...
If he didn’t come back...
She wouldn’t be able to survive, even if it was his last wish.
And last, but not least, was Sharnoth.
She was sitting on the floor, right next to the bed, her body was still, but her fingers moved strangely against the carpet, drawing patterns that made no sense.
The cold, calculating, shrewd Sharnoth had already buried herself deep inside her mind, the wild, chaotic Sharnoth had taken over the body.
And...
She had been silent for hours.
Yes, even Sharnoth, who thought torture was a play date, who sang as she attacked her enemies, and laughed all the time at the silliest of things—
She was silent.
Then suddenly, she stood up.
For a moment, no one reacted to her, every woman had been doing their own thing all this while, without anyone interrupting anyone.
However, the moment Sharnoth walked towards the door, Evane looked at her and frowned.
"Sister Sharnoth, where are you going?"
She asked.
Sharnoth paused for a moment, then she looked at her and—
"To bring him back."
She spoke with an absolutely serious look on her face and that took Evane aback.
When had she seen Sharnoth talk without a crazy, distorted grin on her face...?
She couldn’t recall.
This was the woman who faced her worst enemy with a grin so wide that it was actually concerning, even when the battle wasn’t going according to how she wanted, even if she was losing—
Her smile never faded away.
Until today.
"To... bring him back...?"
Evane raised her eyebrows.
"Of course."
Evane didn’t know what she was supposed to say, Sharnoth didn’t care, she was about to leave when—
"Bring him back? You think this is a joke?"
Riona, who had been trying to hold herself together, for herself, for Amaya, for her son Caelum, grandson Orion, and other children who weren’t exactly hers but she still treated them as her own—
She snapped.
"He is dead!"
She screamed.
"He was surrounded by the five strongest beings in the Universe, he was forced to fight them alone while every single one of us was in here, watching it happen right in front of our eyes!
It happened!
He was surrounded!
He was killed!
And he was killed right in front of our eyes!
And there is nothing you can do about it!
Get it through your head!!"

That scream got a reaction out of every single person in the room, Evane was quick to create a barrier, making sure the children did not hear what Riona said, however, as those words rang in her head, her heart squeezed, tears streamed down her eyes and this time, she couldn’t hide it.
But she wasn’t alone.
Riona’s words refreshed the memory the women were trying to bury deep in their hearts, their tears that had barely dried up returned.
Riona herself was no different, she too, was crying as she glared at Sharnoth, as for Sharnoth—
"I’ll undo his death."
She spoke with a serious look on her face.
"I will absorb Zylarith and learn how to undo his death."
She repeated.
"HAVE YOU LOST YOU—"
Her words only flared Riona’s anger even further but then—
"I’ll come with you."
Amaya, who was standing right beside her, spoke up as she began walking towards her.
"What...?"
Riona blinked.
"You have all lost your minds."
Ember laughed, grabbing the women’s attention.
"Bring him back? From where? Do you even understand what beingerasedmeans?"
Amaya did not like her attitude—
"At least we are trying to do something."
She countered.
"Unlike you."
"Yes, of course. Trying to do something. A little late for that, don’t you think? Where was this spirit when he was fighting out there alone?"
The Dragon asked in a mocking tone, the look on her face however, made it clear that she wasn’t mocking Amaya, she was mocking herself.
But—
Amaya wasn’t in the right state to notice that.
So she—
"You have a death wish, don’t you?"
She spoke, the dark, dense devouring energy around her becoming threatening.
"I do.
What can you do about it? Fulfil it? You can’t even do that, let alone bring him back."
Ember taunted, almost as if she wanted Amaya to kill her.
And Amaya—
BOOOOOOOOOM
The Devouring Energy around her exploded.
Now normally, this would be the moment where the rest of the women would have stood up to stop them.
But this time—
No one did, not even Evane.
Almost as if whatever happened didn’t concern them. If anything, they were hoping for something to happen, for someone to die—
At least that way, they wouldn’t be the first to go against Nux’s last words.
It would give them an excuse to end themselves as well.
With that thought in their minds, some of the women actually released their own Energy, almost as if they were letting out all their built-up frustration and despair.
BOOOOOOOM
More and more energies collided.

For some reason, even when these energies collided, none of it moved towards the bed where the children were, almost as if even when their minds were broken, even as they had lost all their self-control—
The women still actively protected their children.
But—
That protection didn’t seem to do anything when they themselves were about to tear each other’s throats apart.
The chaos became stronger as more and more energies collided and then suddenly—
Zzzzpp
All Energies disappeared as if they had never existed and suddenly—
Lane’s expression changed as she sensed something.

chapters.title: Chapter 2389: Please... please be Nux...
paragraphs: Just as the women were about to have a go at each other to take their built-up frustration out—
Zzzzpp
All Energies in the room disappeared as if they had never existed.
The women froze, shocked by what had happened. Shadow’s expression hardened as she sensed something and warned the rest.
"Someone’s forcing their way into the Universe."

She tried to resist, to keep whatever entity it was outside, but it wasn’t working. There was no ’defense mechanism’ built in the Universe, or a Wall she could simply strengthen to stop whatever was coming.
There was honestly nothing she could do.
It was either an Entity could come inside, or not.
And right now—
It seemed like itwascoming.

Hearing her words, the women’s expressions turned solemn too, even Astaria and Vyriana, who hadn’t participated in the chaos because they had given up on their will to fight suddenly stood straight, their eyes narrowing dangerously.
They may have made a decision to not fight, but when it came to their children’s safety, it was an entirely different matter.
And the rest of the women were the same.
No matter how broken they were.

When the enemy was coming in, they were all ready to face him, together. All of them took their battle stance and prepared for the worst, Shadow turned towards the children and tried to use the Power of Space to send them away.
But just then—
Lane, who had taken her sword out and had extended her senses to the maximum, making sure the enemy didn’t take her by surprise—
Noticed a movement right beneath her.
Her Shadow—
It was moving.
Or more accurately, it was trembling. In the same way as when...
Lane called out, a little confused.
"Huh?"
"What?"
The rest of the women reacted strongly at their husband’s name, but before they could understand what Lane was trying to say—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE

The entire Universe trembled, Shadow’s eyes widened in surprise, she had no clue what was happening. She tried to spread her energy to calm the Universe down, to tell it she and the others were still here.
But suddenly—
Shadow froze.
She lost her Authority over the Universe.
As if... the Universe itself deemed her less worthy and gave itself to someone more worthy.
"Who is it?"
Shadow’s face distorted as her eyes looked around, glowing with anger.
The rest of the women were now even more confused but—
RUMBLE RUMBLE RUMBLE
The Universe shook again, this time, stronger than before. Then suddenly—
"COME OUT YOU BASTARD!!!"
Shadow screamed.
The rest of the women turned towards her, this time, more alert than before.
"Shadow, what’s wrong?"
Vyriana questioned.
"S-Someone’s devouring the Universe’s resources."
"Resources?"
"Five Worlds just vanished."
Shadow answered and the women’s eyes widened in horror.
"The enemy was already here?"
Astaria had already grabbed her sword.
But then—
"It is not an enemy!"
Lane spoke, much louder than any of the women here had heard her speak, but Lane didn’t care, she looked at Astaria, then at Shadow, with her dark eyes shining with strong excitement and—
"It’s Nux! He’s back!!"
She informed as she pointed at her shadow that was still trembling softly.
The women frowned, especially Shadow, after all, the two of them were saying the exact opposite things.
Shadow wondered out loud, her mind was then jolted awake as she started thinking.
It made sense.
She had been panicking becausesomeonewas taking control over the Universe Nux gave her.
But—
This was the Universe Nuxgaveher. She, his wife, inherited it from him and no being would be able to take it from her, no matter how strong they were.
So when the Universe was beingtaken awayfrom her.
There was only one logical answer.
It was Nux.
And it wasn’t himtaking awaythe Universe, it was the Universe reacting to his presence andreturningto him.
Like it was supposed to.
"Yes! It’s Nux! My Shadow only trembles in that manner when Nux is reforming his body to appear next to me!"
Lane exclaimed, her tears streamed down her eyes, but this time, the emotion these tears were carrying wasn’t sadness.
It was relief.
Relief and happiness so strong that her mind couldn’t completely process it.
The rest of the women stared at Lane’s Shadow and as if answering those gazes—
The Shadow rose.
Unlike how it almost instantly turned into Nux in a matter of seconds, this time, the process was... a lot slower than usual.
And that was when Shadow realized it—
"He is using the Universe’s resources to reform his body."
She commented.
"So the five worlds you mentioned before..."
Lyriana asked in a low, uncertain, but hopeful voice.
"Yes, it was him."
Shadow nodded.

Even now, she still wasn’t absolutely sure since none of the women here could sense it, even Lane had only recognized the pattern. It was like listening to someone’s footsteps and assuming who it was.
The only difference was Lane wouldn’t mistake it, or at least, she was absolutely sure she wouldn’t mistake it.
But the rest of the women were still prepared.
Their children were here, they couldn’t take any risk, so they were prepared to move the moment they realized it wasn’t Nux but someone trying to copy him.
However, as suspicious as they were.
The women’s eyes had changed.
Hope.
A terrifyingly strong, almost painful hope.
"And he’s... devouring more..."
Shadow mentioned as she sensed three more worlds disappear out of existence.
These were the worlds Nux had devoured for the future, worlds that their children were supposed to use to get stronger, worlds they had saved as a form of ’resources’.
And this action made Shadow doubt herself and Lane.
Was it... truly Nux?
Would he truly use resources he had saved for his children to... return...?
She wondered in her head.

But then she looked at the women around her, the tears in their eyes, their half-broken state, then her eyes fell on a dark, tinted window that reflected her own face, which was no better than the others.
And she got the answer.
He would.
If it was for his wives, Nux would do anything.
Please... please be Nux...
Shadow muttered as she stared at the thin black thread that originated from Lane’s shadow, flicking non-stop as if it was doing everything it could to survive.
